The modules are quick bursts of education and so insightful. This app is so wonderful and comforting for the distress that comes with ADHD. Thank you
author: BDizzle1ful

title: Is this the only way to get a refund?
body: For a company that focuses on supporting ADHD you really don’t seem to care about good process. Trying to get a refund is IMPOSSIBLE. I signed up for Inflow over 12 months ago - paid for 12 months access, rarely used the app as didn’t find benefit, got a new phone, never logged back in. Fast forward to a few weeks ago when a $284 charge pops up in my card for Inflow. No prior comms/reminders on upcoming renewal (I’ve searched everywhere) just a big fat payment taken from my account. Great. Go hunting for how to contact/get a refund/cancel my account - not easy to find as not on the App, it’s on a website. Have to figure out login details etc. Finally work it all out - send email as instructed. No response. Send follow up. Still no response. Seriously. Come to the App Store to see if there are any other contact options - find out this appears to be a VERY common issue. Am now assuming this is your profit strategy. Seriously. Do better.

author: Amber Knight

title: Little by little
body: I found Inflow really helpful, in that it teaches you to look at why and how you are procrastinating( that is my main problem but they do focus on other similar mental health type issues). It then helps you to work on very small ways to change things around and is very encouraging as you go. It is a fantastic help, unfortunately I couldn’t continue on with it due to my financial situation but the lessons I DID do opened my eyes enormously! I would thoroughly recommend it to anyone to give it a try!

title: Amazing

I love that the app lets you know it’s ok not to get it right every time straight away and that change takes time and that it’s ok to make a mistake. author: Chazwazza178

title: Inflow is the core resource and a very powerful habit for me.
body:
Inflow has proven to be a core resource for me as I learn to live with my ADHD. A diagnosis that continues to make me question who I am, how I got to where I am in life, and how the world works around me. Inflow’s structure with daily learning modules is steadily increasing my understanding of ADHD. It explains why I have endured such confusion and suffering throughout my life (I was diagnosed at 58!) Inflow provides me with strategies that I can actually understand, that I can logically accept and that I increasingly use in most aspects of my daily life. It hasn’t cured me (ha ha) but I do know more about why I do things the way I do. 
Amazingly I am still doing Inflow most every day, that is, for more than 2 months which is an achievement that only people with ADHD would appreciate. That’s a great achievement for me. The appbmust be structured just for us, and is rewarding enough for me to remain engaged and not to get distracted by something “shiny” elsewhere.  
The inflow app continues to be a crucial resource, for me, in my attempts to reduce the ADHD related suffering affecting me and those around me, my family and work mates .
Unexpectedly, there are other insights. For example I have also developed a degree of compassion for myself -both in the here and now, and also for myself in the past, as a child, a teenager, and throughout my adult life. I also increasingly understand why the people in my story responded the way they did. 
I strongly recommend investing in this program  to the people like myself who are genuinely confused and overwhelmed by their diagnosis that may have caused them to question everything that they thought they knew about themselves and the world around them.
In all honesty, I have to say that at first I was hesitant to start the app. Financially it was a big commitment. And would Ibstay the course?  However, based on my positive experience with the Additude website, combined with the usual overwhelming, in the moment, impulse to do the program, I swept this hesitation aside and pressed the “GET”  button. 
It costs me about about a $1 AUD a day. Much less than my mild online shopping habit and  I think it is well worth it. I do the modules-virtually every day-and has it has proved to be a rewarding and valuable part of my new routine.
Inflow has, I believe,  proven to be, for me, a significant, meaningful and positive new habit. It is a learning experience that is practical and applicable to my daily activities. It is as you might say “real world friendly” 

This is a genuine review- I am a real person. I am not being paid to write this. 

( although I wouldn’t turn down any little presents from George and the gang.)

author: Velocityx101

title: Pretty Good
body:
I’d give this app four and a half stars, but it could be a five. 

This app is really good and is the best all rounder for ADHD in my opinion. Price is no issue when trying to better myself so that is not important in my opinion. But I do validate the reason for others.

My main feedback is to have a better locking system for the modules. This prevents someone like me, and I’m sure others from unlocking other tasks and modules in advance. Maybe the one week free trial is good for this exploration and I need some restraint for myself. But checking in each day and tasks being locked until the following day is a good idea as it gives you a goal or something to consider during that one day. For example, in the module with the launchpad, you could have the next days module locked so you can do it or at least think about it/have a creative solution like this. I know the app has a  “challenges” section and this is really good, but these should be imbedded within the module after the quiz. That way you can visually see it after completing the module and then it takes you to the challenges section when you click on it. 

I’m thinking of another app that does this well that I believe this app could benefit from. Just something to take into consideration with experimentation of the functions. However, overall this app has the best content which I’m happy with regardless. 

Good job.

title: Very helpful
body: I’ve struggled with managing my emotions most of my life. Sometimes you don’t even realise some of the behaviours that you exhibit until they’re pointed out to you. The modules have taught me a lot and having a coach available to bounce ideas off and hold you accountable is a bonus. A paid for 1 year and it ended up costing me less than a 1 hour session with a therapist. Absolutely worth the money.

author: PenguinFlea

title: Adult ADHD user experience
body:
I feel really optimistic about this app from what I’ve already experienced. 

If you are serious about managing aspects of tour ADHD then this is worth your time and money. 

I really enjoy how the learning is delivered - bite sized and easy to implement. Most importantly great ideas to help the new habit stick. After all ADHD people always have great ideas, just can’t remember what we were implementing the next day.

This is the real deal but those that will value this app will be People who are serious about wanting help and aren’t just looking for ‘cheap’ solutions. 

It’s a five star rating from me. Well done to the people behind it. And thank you for your passion and expertise that has gone into this.
author: Dani gb

title: The Best!
body: For years I’ve been looking for the ‘killer app’ for ADHD. I’ve found it. I use this daily and work with a real life human coach. It’s jam packed with good stuff. Great self and guided coaching, insights and more content than I think I could consume in a lifetime. So many apps are just along for the ride with the ADHD community: generalized apps marketing themselves to everybody including people with ADHD. But they are focused on ADHD. Inflow IS. It’s gold. Highly highly recommend it. A superb investment.

author: nick-626

title: The Carrot and The Stick
body:
The Carrot
Manage your ADHD in 5 minutes a day

The Stick
Too expensive without a decent look behind the curtain first, and by decent I mean longer than 7 days. I am the father of a family of 4, all of us have ADHD. It's crazy in my house and we all have different needs. I can't afford 4 accounts to keep us all sane. The numbers just don't stack up. Speaking of which is it $33/mth USD or AUD? I have no way of knowing? And if you multiply that by x4 it blows out to a massive USD $132/mth or AUD $185/mth for my family, either way NOT A CHANCE I would pay for either. Sorry.

This app could be useful, if I knew more about what it actually does up front. Give users a bigger carrot and you're more likely to get my money. I totally understand you have a team of BA's, QA's, Engineers, UX, UI etc to pay for but sadly your trial is too short and the price point is too high. I have deleted my account. 

So here's a User Story for you to take back to your team:
As a... parent and family with ADHD 
I want... a better opportunity to see the benefits of the app with affordable access 
So that... my family's ADHD can be managed better together

All the best

body:

author: Elevas

title: A fair price for the service provided
body:
This app is like headspace for headcases. Clearly a lot of love has gone into building this app and there seems to be a lot of clinical research backing it. As such I think it’s entirely fair for this to be a paid product. 

Another review said that the price was too high and that subscription services are an ADHD trap, yet one of the first things you see in the onboarding is “we will refund you if you forget to cancel”. Some people are rather ungrateful, and I can say I am grateful that the education around ADHD is improving, and I’m glad this service exists.

author: xoxox0x0

title: Highway Robbery Disguised as Help!
body:
Paying €49.99 a month for Inflow? That’s downright disgusting! The cheapest plan at €229.99 a year is just RIDICULOUS. Can't afford the OUTRAGEOUS yearly subscription at once? Choose the monthly plan and you're throwing away €600 a year 😂🔫. For that price, I can subscribe to Apple TV+, Apple Arcade, Apple Music, iCloud (all for €19.95 a month), Netflix (€9.99 a month), Disney+ (€9.15 a month), and Amazon Prime (€4.99 a month) and still have €5 left each month to splurge on whatever I want. 

 Clearly, you have to be a sociopath to think this is fair pricing. This app takes advantage of those in need without offering anything spectacularly different from cheaper (or free) alternatives. 

 Pricing Predators Preying on ADHD! 

 Repulsive.
author: TechnoToken3000

title: Truly helpful for understanding my ADHD
body:
Inflow has been incredibly important in this challenging moment of my life. While dealing with serious family health issues and managing my own ADHD, this app has helped me understand every nuance of how ADHD affects my day, my focus, emotions, habits, and energy.

What makes it unique is how practical and personal it feels. Each lesson helps me recognize patterns in real time, and talking to Quinn, the AI coach, not only gives me strategies I can actually use, but also provides a safe space to talk, open up emotionally, and understand what to do with those feelings.

It’s not just information it’s support. For anyone with ADHD who wants real, everyday tools, Inflow makes a meaningful difference.
author: Almeida 18 aí

title: De grande ajuda
body:
Baixei o app sem muitas expectativas. Fui recém-diagnosticada com TDAH e nunca tinha estudado sobre o assunto. Então, para mim, foi uma grata surpresa ver o conteúdo que o app oferece. Os módulos são curtos e direto-ao-ponto, esclarece situações típicas que os neurodivergentes enfrentam e ensina técnicas muito simples e efetivas para melhorar a qualidade de vida e o "funcionamento" de quem sofre dessa condição. Às vezes é um pouco embaraçoso ver como é necessário usar linguagem e motivacional quase infantil com o usuário do app, mas para a grande maioria, com certeza tem um impacto emocional positivo. Como os outros, também levei um susto com a anuidade do app, mas considerando que muitas coisas não são automatizadas e dependem da ação de uma equipe humana, ao fim me pareceu um preço bem razoável - pra quem não consegue pagar um acocuntability coach para acompanhamento, é um substituto interessante.

Por depender de uma equipe humana de profissionais da área, o pleno usufruto do app exige domínio do inglês. Para quem se garante na língua, o inflow é uma boa ferramenta.

title: Frustrating app experience, non existent support
body:
TL;DR: ADHD newbies might like the app for a bit, but not ‘veterans’—but you should *really* stay away from the app for its abysmal support. Once they have your money, you’re on your own. Yet another way to exploit the neurodivergent.

I’ll give it a star as I could see how this could be helpful if you’re newly diagnosed or only just looking into ADHD… and because I have to. 

That said, the bit of very basic information that you *have* to go through to even just check the app’s features out didn’t instil hope in me in terms of the app’s effectiveness or depth, and another AI chatbot isn’t a tool I need in my toolbox.

The real issue is the complete lack of support though, especially in regard to billing and cancellations. I still have yet to hear back from their support team and had to manage everything on my own (and this took me months, partly because I HAVE ADHD), and have read that this is a VERY common complaint.

Does a team even exist outside of responding to app feedback here? Because you sure don’t respond to emails at the address you keep providing people with 😬

EDIT: No, I will NOT email you at the same email address that you’ve ignored my previous emails. Do better.

title: Recycled lifehacks and AI, waste of money plus constant emails
body:
The module on Task Avoidance is literally just first-page-of-google results: “break it into smaller steps,” pomodoro, Eisenhower matrix, SMART goals. 
Great, I tried all of these things for years when I didn’t know I had ADHD. They’re not built for ADHD brains. 
Once you complete the module, it directs you to an obsequious AI chatbot that offers nothing more than ChatGPT for free. 

I’m so disappointed an app with resources and professionals is using predatory marketing to reel in people with ADHD who are seeking help, only to force you into a locked path of the most basic “life hacks” you’ve already tried. 

Bonus: it also gives you a new task to avoid! I got 20 emails from Inflow during my trial. TWENTY. Ridiculous. 

Don’t waste your time. Hope this saves someone else the feelings of defeat and disappointment.

title: Good for beginners, but a bit disappointing.
body:
I have AuDHD, and I’m also a therapist who specializes in supporting neurodivergent individuals, particularly those who are ADHD &/or autistic. So I am often looking for new tools and supports for myself and my clients. When completing the quiz, I indicated a high level of existing knowledge, and Inflow still indicated that I would learn lots, so I decided to try it out. While I recognize not everyone is an AuDHD therapist specializing in these areas, I know many with ADHD or AuDHD typically hyperfixate when suspecting or finding out about their diagnosis, and will often come across most of the information and tools from Inflow within their first year of suspecting/finding out. You may find a point or strategy here or there that may be new and helpful to you, and the community aspect may appeal to you, but I mostly wouldn’t recommend this unless you are newly suspecting/diagnosed. This is an absolutely wonderful resource for those who are totally new to exploring ADHD info and tools, but may be disappointing and disheartening for those that have have been struggling to find helpful supports for longer, as this could feel like another deadend of info they already know. I appreciate this as a resource, but I think Inflow should consider letting people know from the start that it may likely be more helpful for those newer to their diagnosis and who haven’t already hyperfixated on investigating tools and supports so they don’t spend valuable time & energy (which we know is even more valuable in ADHD world). Otherwise, I really do recognize value here for those who may just be starting to dive in to ADHD.

One other aspect I wanted to mention that is something I am more critical of, is the “check-in” feature that asks some questions at the beginning and end of a module to see how you’ve supposedly improved. However, the questions they ask at the end are not the same ones asked at the beginning. The check-in questions at the beginning of the modules are to gauge your level of difficulty with certain tasks/situations, the questions they ask after the modules are to gauge how well certain things went in the past week in a more specific way. The results then indicate a huge leap in improvement, when that is not possible to entirely determine from this method of checking-in. This is partially because asking how poorly someone is doing with something vs how well they are doing will give you different answers based on the wording and perception of the questions asked. I was asked after the modules how often I was able to use certain methods to support an executive functioning difficulty, but I was already using some of these methods prior to completing the module, so if they asked me those same questions BEFORE the module, my answers would have been the same. Instead, I was asked more general questions in the beginning about my level of difficulty with tasks, and at the end, more specific questions that were more about what I was able to do that week. If they asked the exact same questions at beginning and end, this would give a far more accurate indication of improvement. This was an aspect that really disappointed me because it gives people a false understanding of their progress, and a false understanding of what has been most helpful for them and what hasn’t.

title: Supportive and Easy to Use
body: I have used InFlow for the past two months since I was diagnosed with ADHD at age 40. I have found the modules to be curated for what I need, based on a quiz when you first sign up. And I can’t access the other modules until I’ve finished mine (great for my ADHD distraction lol). The lessons are easy to follow and the key ideas and brain hacks from each lesson help to solidify the messages, because you can book mark those tidbits. I LOVE the live focus rooms on Zoom for support and staying accountable for workdays or household tasks. The hosts are lovely and knowledgeable. It’s nice to know I am not alone! And the community “question of the day” is great for quick check ins and discussion with limits on how much you can write. Again. Perfect for ADHD brain 😆

title: I didn’t love this as much as I wanted to.
body: I am desperate to figure out how to manage my ADHD. I wanted this app to change my life. Unfortunately, it didn’t meet my expectations. If you’re someone who has investigated other tools, chances are that none of the info will be new. The most painful part for me is that the most frequent tip is to journal, or write it down. My executive functions are deficient; I am terrible at time management. Finding time to journal or write it down and reflect is often a time consuming and stress-inducing task. When I end up not journaling every emotion, I will be overcome with feelings of failure and shame. This just isn’t the tool for me.

author: DooDa222

title: Doesn’t live up to it’s word
body:
I am pretty disappointed with this company because going in they make promises that they don’t keep. I did the 7 day trial which is not enough time for a person with ADHD to get a feel for whether it is something they can commit too. 

It seemed really promising and so I didn’t cancel and ended up paying the full year subscription. It is not cheap but I felt hopeful that it would be worth it. I did well in staying committed for two weeks but then something disrupted the routine and I started to struggle with even remembering that I had the app let alone that I paid a few hundred dollars for it. 

The biggest selling point for me was that there was the mentors that you speak with to help you and I was open about my struggles with the app with then. But one day that options was just gone. I went to message the person and couldn’t find our chat and haven’t been able to since. Contacted support and never heard back from them!!

Another selling point was that they seemed understanding of how ADHD works and committed to offering refunds anytime no questions. I wrote support to talk about getting at least a partial refund because I just wasn’t receiving any value from the app, it just wasn’t working for me. I never heard back from them.  This is a gigantic red flag and I really regret spending the money. 

I would proceed with caution before giving any money to a company as inconsistent as this one.

body:

author: skirt Justice

title: Probably best for newly diagnosed
body:
I was really excited to try this app as I’ve been having some serious struggles getting back into a rhythm post-pandemic. Based on the description I had thought this app would help on organization, creating structure, accountability, and inspiration/motivation as an ADHD specific planner tool…. But it’s more like an info resource to learn about ADHD and your own presentation or challenges. Definitely has some interesting content and provides a good summary of everything available on the web/in books without having to wade through the junk on your own.

The included coaching is pretty basic and was not useful for me, I found the check-ins to be circular questions that became frustrating and annoying so I ignored that feature after 3 months. Didn’t try the one-on-one virtual coaching due to cost, it’s was more expensive than the IRL coaching I’ve done. Live events are all scheduled during my work hours, but replays and transcripts are available. Interesting content and some good discussions, again most likely beneficial for people recently diagnosed.

Overall, best for people diagnosed within 1-2 years looking for information. Recommend changing the description from a ‘managing’ ADHD app to an ‘educational’ ADHD app.

body:

I also found myself thinking of it as another thing to do and feeling guilt about the money I paid and that I wasn’t using it enough and that made me avoid it even more. I really appreciate the work everyone put in and It’s really interesting if you haven’t gone into a hyperfocus about adhd and want to learn more but I found myself adding it to my to do list and then moving it to the next day because it came down to this or meditation. 

Im still looking for a place that has stuff like a super easy day planner, a place to store really easy reliable meals, an adhd friendly a place to get interesting tips like those that I often find on “how to adhd” about things like the “wall of awful”, adhd friendly meditation, some focus building games, a task timer, or even maybe some lessons that explain the neuroscience behind adhd.

author: CurlSquirrel

title: Sad to read
body:
Was excited to try this app. Having read the reports about the extreme price paired with the auto billing after a free trial though this has turned me right off and now I won’t touch it. If your app is really intended to help people with Adhd this process needs to be rethought or unfortunately you just come off like you’re taking advantage of some of a major ADHD vulnerability for profit.  Just another kick in the face. I’m not saying you don’t deserve to make money from your work or service, seems like a great app, but this is basically baiting and then using clients disability against them. That’s messed up.
alternative examples:
-daily countdown synced to email during trial period + extremely straightforward process to deregister. That would show respect.
-some free content + tour of pro content features without usability until payment
-pay when you’re ready to upgrade then after payment can trial the features for 2-4 days and if it’s not a good fit there’s an option for money back in this period. (Basically the same as a trial and trust me you’d still make money here but at least it’s not forcing a pending direct auto bill at time
of download)
author: hereiamlately

title: Know your customer
body:
I started this free trial after hearing about this app and wanted to check it out. The content is pretty decent and helpful. I am however very disappointed that after the 7 day free trial, you are automatically charged the most expensive option of a 1 year subscription with coaching ($300+). This shows a lot of disrespect to the intended audience of this app who are very likely to forget to cancel. Talk about taking advantage of the ADHD tax. 

If this happens to you, don’t worry. You can go through the Apple to get a refund. I got one within 24 hours. 

The monthly is also a little bit on the pricy side but  I honestly would have paid the monthly amount for a little while longer to see if it helped me manage adhd. Unfortunately, this experience left a bad taste in my mouth and I won’t be re-subscribing. I hope you consider changing this practice.

body: I am really enjoying the app so far, but I have a slight problem with how the app is formatted to begin with. Read ADHD books like “Order from Chaos” by Jaclyn Paul; “Getting Things Done” by David Allen; anything by Russell Barkley, including his lectures that are free on YouTube. These are much more useful resources than this garbage.

I am learning how to become more organized and reliable, not only to others but to myself as well. I actually feel hopeful about functioning at a level I didn’t think was possible before. The daily prompts are clear, super short, and offer actionable steps to apply what you learn. I feel freedom to go at my own pace & actually WANT to keep going. Even if I go a week or two without using the app I feel like I can jump right back to where I left off in the program, continuing to learn and grow. I’m really grateful for this resource in managing my inattentive ADHD symptoms.

title: Information on adhd in women very Basic
body:
I’m really disappointed in the material on women with ADHD. It is labelled as „unique experience“ and hidden in the app, even though you are asked in the survey about your gender and how you indentify. The focus in that category is almost entirely on partnerships and children, as if women were only meant to have babies and boyfriends and that’s all we could possibly want. Only a few sentences acknowledge the broader reality of women who live independently or choose different paths.

Just because many of your clients may be in their 40s with children does not mean this represents all women struggling with adhd. The material could have been structured to reflect different life situations. What about women in their teens, 20s, or those in their 30s, who don’t want children or a partner - regardless of being heterosexual? Not to mention the queer community. Much of what you present here can already be found in countless ADHD podcasts. In fact, some podcasts hosted by men cover women’s ADHD experiences more thoughtfully than this app does.

It’s 2025, and yet you’re still reproducing outdated gender roles while presenting yourself as knowledgeable about ADHD in women. And when it comes to men, the conversation doesn’t immediately revolve around household chores or children or EVEN partnerships. What a coincidence.

The material on hormones and ADHD is also extremely limited. The explanation is not really detailed and very basic. Not really more on the science on PMDD and hormonal cycles in general. If you really want to understand how to manage your hormonal cycle you need to search elsewhere for further information. There are no meaningful, practical tips on how to manage ADHD symptoms throughout the cycle besides some essential oils (don’t get me wrong oils can help).

body:

This particular e-Mail also said that I was being charged if I didn’t cancel the subscription within 24 hours. Obviously I didn’t cancel (people with ADHD can be very forgetful) because I read the mail too late. 
Let’s see where this goes:) 
In general, I’d also say that the app is absolutely overpriced and for the most part useless, since you might as well go to therapy and have actual face to face conversations for the high prices they charge.

title: Very confusing pricing
body:

Monthly/annual without coaching is listed twice with different prices for the exact same thing and once with coaching. Also 6 month with coaching is available for 230€ while annual with coaching is only 215€. (Why would anyone take 6 month?)
For an app that tries to help people with ADHD this is very confusing.
The app seems great but I would love a clear communication about prices before I subscribe. Maybe ask one of the mental health professionals you employ for help with the design of the pricing tables.

body:

But this app is Too expensive, approximately 350 DKK per month.

I’d get the idea with acces to professional help in the app - but I’d love if it was possible to subscribe to a version without the vast (and very impressing!) extra “perks”.

Also because , while I’m that privileged to live a place where people with disabilities can actually get help through our national taxed health care system (with exactly learning me how to execute etc), affordable medication etc.,  plus, I’ve done a lot to understand my “trigger” points etc (but being nerdy also helps psycho-education). 

But I have  no doubt that this app could make a great and vital difference for many people but who might couldn’t spare that cost in budget to put into this app.

Well that was LONG, if you read through: thanks 🙏

author: M0M 0F 4

title: Preying on ADHD people. Beware
body:
What a shame. I really wanted to like this app and hoped it could make a real difference on how I manage my adhd symptoms. However following my experience with them, I cannot reach any other conclusion than thinking they are actually targeting the community they are supposed to help. 
In a few words, I tried the app for 2 solid months then decided it wasn’t working for me and cancelled my subscription. However instead of going ahead with it they sneakily stopped taking payments from my PayPal account and instead switched to taking payments directly through my bank debit card. This, without my consent or even informing me. I ended up paying an extra £364 over 13 months without realising it. When I asked them for a refund they just offered to refund 1 month - £28. Now I just spent 5 hours researching legal recourse, building my case and talking to my bank in the hope of getting my money back. And it’s just the beginning. How is that for helping people who naturally struggle handling administrative tasks and often miss details? I would say they are doing pretty well using their understanding of ADHD symptoms… against us. Please just beware.

Update: I was eventually given a full refund so I raise my rating a bit. However it took a lot of efforts and hours of complaining to the right places. And the cancellation process is still too unintuitive. I understand the need to generate income for startups but as an app for ADHDers, if you are really serious about helping us, ease of use and transparency about payments should be in your DNA. Please do better.

title: Worth every penny.
body:
I have referred SO many of my friends to this app! 

I got curious if I had ADHD after struggling with what I call ‘chronic procrastination’. Unavoidable, crippling procrastination. Of work, of sleep, of contacting friends. 

While I was waiting for my diagnosis, I decided to try the app because if the shoe fits and it helps me, what’s the relevance of if I do or don’t have ADHD? (Spoiler: I do). 

If I could break my journey to where I am now down and how much better I can now work WITH and understand my adhd, this app contributed 70% of it. Easily.  

In the last 3 years, I’ve spent £10k on therapy and coaching from neuro divergent specialists, and that got me an extra 20% of the way. 

On reflection, it made me realise just how this app is worth every penny. 
I truly hope anyone reading this gives it a go and gets as much out of it as I have. 

One word of advice. You can lead a horse to water but you can’t force it drink. Ie. You get out of this app what you put in.
At least that’s what I found. 

All the best on your journey. It really is a gift to have adhd - even if it doesn’t always feel like it 🙏🏼

author: Anonymous 773

title: Predatory Free Trial - Be Careful
body:
Out of every free trial I’ve ever signed up for, this one has the most complex and misleading cancellation process. This is particularly alarming for an app that is supposedly founded and developed by experts in ADHD - and it’s clearly intentional because when they try to get you to sign up, they acknowledge that people with ADHD are more likely forget about their subscriptions and reassure you that they won’t let that happen. 

You might think that I’m exaggerating about how ridiculous the cancellation process is, but I assure you I’m not. Let me lay out the step-by-step process:

1. On the app, navigate to the ‘You’ page.

2. Click on the settings icon.

3. Now click on ‘Account 
Management and Help’. This opens up a separate webpage.

4. You now have to click on a link titled ‘How can I cancel my inflow subscription or free trial?’.

5. On this page, it gives 4-step instructions for cancelling your subscription. It fails to mention that there are more steps after the 4th step.

6. They also decide to mention here for the first time that if your trial ends in less than 24 hours, you can’t cancel it and you will be charged. There is no mention of this policy when signing up for the trial. In fact, it specifically states on the checkout page that you will be “Billed after your trial ends, unless cancelled before your renewal date.” which is objectively false - as you have to cancel one day before your renewal date to avoid being billed. 

If you are billed, you will have to now email them to request a refund. Despite claiming during the sign-up process that they’ll refund you if you forget to cancel your free trial, they fail to mention that you’re not entitled to a refund if you use the app after the renewal date - which most people likely will do if they don’t realise they’re trial has ended. Conveniently, they can also take up to 2 business days to respond to your refund request, meaning if you request a refund within the last 24 hours of your trial, but then use the app the next day while waiting for a response - you won’t be refunded.

7. If you’re lucky enough to be cancelling within the first 6 days - you now have to click a link to a new page called your ‘subscription portal’.

8. In this portal, you have to re-login using the password you made when you signed up. Many people will have forgotten it so they’ll have to reset it by questing a code by email. Weirdly, when I first logged into the app - I wasn’t asked if I wanted to ‘remember my password’ which I found odd - but I’m not sure if this was just my experience or the sign-up process is designed that way intentionally.

9. Once you’ve managed to log-in, click on the ‘manage my subscription’ heading for a new page with different options.

10. Now you click on the ‘cancel your subscription heading’. This is the 4th and final step listed in the instructions, but the team at inflow thought people with ADHD would appreciate it if the process was even longer, and more tedious - so they added some secret surprise steps. 

11. You now get a new page loaded up, asking if you are absolutely sure you want to cancel. The ‘Keep my subscription’ button is nice and bold, while the ‘cancel’ button is below and blends in perfectly with the background.

12. If you click this cancel button, surely that’s the end of it, right? It seems that way at first as a new page loads up with a “We’re sad to see you go.” message. Awww, how sweet of them to be sad that you’re gone.

13. Well actually, there is nothing to be sad about just yet!!! Because you haven’t gone!!! Your subscription is still not cancelled!!! 

14. You have to scroll down a little before you find the same exact buttons that were on the previous page. Now click ‘cancel’.

14. Another page! With the same two buttons! Click ‘cancel’ again.

15. I can now no longer remember if there were 3 or 4 of these pages in total - it wouldn’t surprise me if it were the latter, but at least now your subscription is actually cancelled, and you will not be billed.

Other subscription services do often make you put in extra effort to cancel, using similar sorts of tactics - but the fact that this was the most confusingly elaborate of them all, with so many opportunities to be mislead is just disturbing.

I suspect that if you looked into the companies financial statements, you’d find that payments from users that no longer use the app is a significant share of their total revenue.

author: alex.hertz

title: Ridiculous advice
body:
“You have ADHD. You struggle with time management. Have you tried… not struggling?” is the gist of every “lesson”. 

Time blindness - oh don’t worry, just get a few more clocks, then you’ll be fine. I don’t struggle to KNOW the time?! I struggle to understand when to move from one task to the next, when it’s too late for me to get somewhere on time… it’s not just “oh look, it’s 4pm, I have an appointment at 4:30pm, best leave now” and the struggle is magically fixed 🤣 

A *real* quote from a lesson I just read is “ADHD doesn’t have to be in the driver’s seat of your life. You can take the wheel now. Where you go next is up to you.” Oh gee, thanks Dr Patronising. Hadn’t thought of that in my silly little ADHD brain. Of course, the answer is just to make different choices!! Doh! 

For £40 / month, I’d expect to at least not be patronised. Do better.
author: Kaylaaa737064280

title: If I could give 0 stars I would
body: This app markets itself as being a management tool for ADHD…so far all I’ve managed to find are condescending “lessons” for me to learn about a condition I’ve had for nearly 40 years!🙄🤣 all I wanted was an efficient calendar and to do list and time management tools all in one app cos no one seems to have come up with that despite telling us “they’re thinking of people who struggle with ADHD” in the design and purpose of this app!🤣 oh and then there are lots of “don’t worry we’ll remind you before we charge you if you forget to cancel your subscription”…then a yearly charge on your card when you think it’s cancelled as they have different sections that you have to navigate your way to in order to do this rather than appearing in Apple subscriptions even if you’ve downloaded the app and paid by Apple Pay!!! When I requested a refund rather than just issuing it I now have had 3 emails and been sent a form to fill in…is your company really tailoring its services to people with ADHD or just targeting them as easy cash?!😡
author: Vix2475

title: Charged me $199.99 despite cancelling before end of trial period
body:
And are now refusing to refund me because the grace period mentioned in their refund policy has passed. Never mind that this is irrelevant since I already cancelled! They claim I didn’t, that they didn’t hear back from me when they sent a reminder email, and that “it's possible that the message ended up in your spam folder”. I actually check my spam folder regularly so I know nothing went there. Besides, none of their emails have ever gone to spam, why this one? And indeed if I didn’t cancel but instead paid $200 for the app - whose material I didn’t find particularly helpful - you’d think I’d at least use it. I only opened it during the trial week and yesterday when I saw the charge on my foreign bank account. They also had the nerve to tell me they’ll offer me a free annual subscription as a way to make up for the frustration. No. I don’t want your app. I didn’t find it helpful so I cancelled before the end of the trial period. You charged me all the same (I’m not alone in this btw). This is the crux of the issue, setting aside reminder emails and regace periods and spam folders and whatnot.
It is unacceptable. I expect I’ll get a developer response rehashing the same claims and offers, instead of doing the single right and sensible thing: refunding me for the hefty fee. I’ll be reporting them.
PS: The fact that there is a) no notification sent pre or post charge (not even a generic email saying “thank you for your subscription, you now have access to abc resources until xyz date” etc) and b) choosing to automatically charge an ANNUAL subscription fee, not monthly, quarterly etc, for an ADHD support app tells you all you need to know about them.

author: Nina.Katya

title: Yeah… no…
body: It’s hard to justify the cost of the subscription when the core of the content is just the same info and tools that you can learn online for free or from any mental health councillor if you see one. Everyone, who’s been trying to address procrastination, messy home, disorganisation and overwhelm, heard about pomodoro technique or SMART goals and chances are, they don’t really work, otherwise there would be no need for yet another app peddling the same tired techniques. No need to pay over 180 quid a year to get the same content. There’s some social aspect to the app but I haven’t explored that other than some daily questions. What this app does is to give you some info and some quizzes about it but if you’re really looking for a good tool to help stay organised and on top of things then I suggest Strides - it’s free, you can trial it for free, you can subscribe for extra templates but what it does, it actually helps you manage your daily life. At least the cancellation process has been fixed and I wasn’t charged after I cancelled the trial.

author: VDisappointed2024

title: Unhelpful
body:
The app hasn’t told me anything I don’t already know under the Burnout module, what I need are the tools to put those things in place. How am I supposed to choose what things can be sacrificed in my life if I don’t have anyone I can delegate tasks to or ask for help? How do I abandon my vulnerable elderly mother with dementia to make “me time”?
It’s unrealistic advice because it assumes that it’s all our own fault and the things we take on can be set aside, but that’s not always the case and there is no deviation in the advice to help you determine what things can be set aside  and what the priorities are. I’m deeply disappointed because I’d really hoped this would be a turning point for me but I’m back at square one.

The app then took the subscription payment from my bank anyway! This has left me very short of funds and waiting the 2 days they take to respond before even generating a refund which will take several days no doubt to come through if they even will agree to a refund. Really disappointed and inconvenienced by the whole thing.
author: Anna.flower

title: Poor CX ruins the app
body: I cancelled this subscription as soon as I set up the trial as I knew I would forget otherwise (and I could always reinstate if needed at a later date). I got very quick confirmation of this being cancelled so was very pleased. It was a busy week so I wasn’t able to utilise the trail, a real shame, yet at the end of the week I was still charged £159(!) I find this really upsetting as I did everything needed to avoid this happening and was told it wouldn’t happen… and still! Very upsetting and I hope I don’t have to wait too much longer for this to be resolved.
author: Mrs_Scarf

title: support system section is bad & subscription is deceptive
body:
absolutely detestable design. apps that don’t tell you it will cost money until you have completed a quiz and should be BANNED. say this on the opening screen. this is deceptive design and not acceptable

also - why is sibling not an option?? or cousin?? these are my main support systems. this should be an option, or people should be able to select “other”. it feels EXTREMELY limiting and VERY exclusionary. allowing an “other” option is UX 101 - this should NOT have made it past going live!!!!!
author: lou23847328943

title: Not ADHD friendly
body: Confusing layout, walls of text, not great for someone with ADHD and a short attention span. Really annoying. I open the app, get overwhelmed with all the stuff it wants me to do and close it. Need to make it more rewarding / dopamine inducing.
author: Appism

title: Do not fall for the Scam!!
body: I did the 1 week trial. Was told by the app it will send reminders to cancel the subscription days before it ends and then never got any reminders. So ofcourse the app then charged me £159. Struggling with ADHD means we’re not going to remember to cancel these sort of things hence the reminders that were needed. They know what they’re doing! Praying on us poor ADHD people to giving them the money. I’ve tried emailing already and requesting a refund but have had no response. I demand a refund. Absolutely useless!
author: JaySlay666

title: Predatory business model. Avoid
body: However much they claim to ‘understand’ people with ADHD, they clearly don’t. A misleading free trial,  NO email reminders when you’re about to be charged (contrary to their claims) and the app is incredibly frustrating to use. Just a terrible experience all round.
author: LKX236

title: Paid only
body:
Don’t be lured in if you don’t have money to burn it’s trying to sell you your mental health for £200 a year or £50 a month. there’s nothing available for people struggling to get by.

*update: you’re committed to profiting from mental health struggles you’re not committed ti helping everyone otherwise you’d include an affordable option, rather than a waiting list/access programme that I bet you would share any stats on about application:award ratios.
author: Nxl Jxb

title: Subscription taken incorrectly
body: I always immediately cancel subscriptions so was shocked when a charge came through.  When I went on the app, it flashed up my subscription was cancelled but when I logged in it was set up for monthly subscriptions.  When I checked on my subscriptions through my iPhone, it isn’t listed as a live or cancelled subscription so I was unable to ensure it was cancelled via subscriptions in my settings.  I would definitely advise against downloading this app unless they have a reasonable explanation for this.  Have asked for my money back but as I can’t see it in descriptions, I am concerned about being charged again next month…
author: ShezzaJane

title: Couldn’t sign up
body: Got through the whole onboarding but only to get an “it’s not you, it’s us” error. If you’re going to create an app for people who have ADHD then sort stuff like this out because some will do exactly what I did - Delete it because it’s too much bother. I’m brilliant at self sabotaging and procrastination - I don’t need an excuse NOT to do something, so this was the perfect reason to dump the app. Doh.
author: Feelgoodhit

title: Difficult to cancel
body: Beware that it’s made difficult to cancel. You can’t do it through the app or from your subscriptions under Apple ID. You must login from the app and then cancel your subscription. It says to do it at least 24 hours before the trial ends which is bizarre?
author: lmn8134

title: Free-trial then take your money
body:
I’ve read a lot of reviews and they say similar things. As an App that tries to help ADHD people, they sure try to put a lot of obstacles to get u a refund and to opt automatically to their full year subscription which is £179 per year and make it difficult for you to get a refund. I asked a refund from Apple last year thinking it went through but realised now that actually it got cancelled and it’s too late now to dispute it. 

I never even used the app not one bit and to be paying £179 as a disabled and unemployed person. That’s an awful lot. Hopefully the app developer will respond to my email and come to a resolution about the refund.
author: mccalling

title: A life saving app
body: This app is genius. So much live accountability. So much bite sized wisdom. So we’ll put together. Everyone needs this app. Especially if you have ADHD. And even if you don’t!
author: The Feline One

title: They won’t stop charging me!!!
body:
I did the trial but cancelled. They charged me anyway then I emailed and they gave me refund and said they cancelled the subscription, and they’ve charged me again. 

I’ve deleted app have no sign of subscription on my phone … idk how to stop them from charging me every month?
author: IHajdjsha

title: Able to be more productive at work
body: I was never officially diagnosed with ADHD but I’ve always been sure I have it, and it clearly runs in my family. The app has allowed me to find a number of ways to be more productive — and that’s made a huge change in my work life.
author: mikeplace

body: I’ve had to cancel my subscription twice now, signed up for free trial but didn’t work for me so cancelled and deleted app. Now found that my subscription hadn’t cancelled and been charged the full amount. Received no reminders to cancel during trial as app says you get, and no emails at all since January, as well as nothing showing in my subscriptions on phone, so naturally assumed it was cancelled. I had to verify my account via email to be able to log in and cancel this time (hopefully actually cancelled this time as still received no confirmation of it) so completely out of pocket for something I won’t use and have two additional charges for payments overseas?! Extremely costly and definitely not worth the price for me.
author: RJD90

title: strange choice of messaging considering the subject
body: Hard to give it a full review as I fell at the first hurdle… after filling out their form confirming demand avoidance and sensitivity to criticism it said it was generating a custom course for me, then the very first page it provided was just  “this time, stick to it”. Needless to say I immediately hated it and closed it 😂
author: J_MC-K

title: Can't cancel in app
body:
Unfortunately I have to rate it down owing to the fact you can't cancel in app or via the my app store profile. This adds extra steps which is fine for me but perhaps not others. Shame I didn't want to as I appericate the affordability scheme they provide. The information is okay but rather basic. I'm sure it may be good for others but not for me. 

On the plus it wasn't difficult to cancel but just not as easy as it could be. Hopefully this minor issue is solved as they clearly do care about their work. author: 183hejr5383

title: no
body: makes you go through lots of questions and then tells you its a paid subscription. go away.
author: snfngnyls

title: Started trial cancelled it and still charged me
body:
This app seems like it waffles along, started the trial and didn’t get as far as getting any help from it. A week is too short. I logged out and removed the app as advised and still charged. No where in the app can you cancel the payment. It’s seems really easy to install and take your money but really difficult to stop the subscription. It’s a con. Please refund me. 

For anyone who needs help in the uk, you can get free government funding for an adhd coach. If you know your adhd type and a decent amount about your it, I found gpt chat is an efficient aid to build a plan. It’s not perfect but it’s free and much much faster than inflow.
author: Aaronembe

title: Subscription needed
body: Installed the app, went through a bunch of info etc only to find you need a subscription to actually use it. More transparency is needed on the app page.
author: Littleowl91

title: Life changing
body: Full disclosure, I was lucky enough to get this app through the access programme as I was struggling with my employment at the time. I wasn’t in a great place, and neither was my mental health. This app has really helped me understand myself and learn how to cope with my ADHD. I’ve been constantly amazed to learn how many things I struggle with aren’t all that unique to me and instead are pretty common symptoms. Daily sessions are just 5 minutes. At first I thought this was a bit insubstantial, but its actually the perfect amount to fit in around a commute and as it doesn’t seem like a big commitment, I’m much more likely to engage on a routine basis. After 9 months of using the app I’ve seen a lot of improvement in aspects of my life such as emotional regulation, time keeping and organisation. My ADHD does still make things harder, but in general I’m far more accepting & forgiving of myself, and my relationships with others are a lot healthier.
author: wilkovic

title: Could not get through the first lesson
body:
The font was ugly, and it’s just way too long…how is this catered to people with adhd. 

UI is confusing.
author: Susoku

title: Not particularly helpful
body: I was hoping for something that could help me overcome my ADHD issues, however the advice and information given was very basic, I have already implemented most of the strategies given and most of them don’t work for me particularly well, there was no alternatives, the advice seems to use the reward theory a lot, but this isn’t helpful if you are not a person who responds to ‘rewards’ and gets no motivation from them. The multi choice questions aren’t particularly multi choice, I regularly found that none of the options described my feelings or situation, all in all I just got more irritated and frustrated the more I tried to work thru the modules. I wouldn’t mind paying for this if it would help in any way but for me there was nothing particularly helpful.
author: katejjjjjjj

title: really working content in bite chunks!
body:
This app is amazing! I was sceptical about that as I've read so much on ADHD and it was hard to find hacks that would really work - this app amused me as most of things there really seem to resonate with me! 
Also it's beautifully done, information is bite chunked, doing just 5 minutes a day in the evening seems to work for me!
author: Alex Turkin

title: Warning: Deceptive Pricing Practices in this App!
body: I installed this app expecting to try out a free trial, but what I encountered was a pricing strategy that left me baffled and frustrated. To access the so-called “free trial,” you’re required to commit to a hefty £180 annual payment, but only if you pay it all at once. If you can’t afford that upfront, be prepared to face an astonishing charge of £516. In essence, it’s £180 for the privileged few and a staggering £516 for the rest of us. And here’s the kicker: if you forget to cancel before the free trial ends, you’ll be hit with unexpected charges. Don’t be fooled by smooth-talking responses from the company. While they claim to offer refunds if you forget to cancel, that might not be a lifeline for everyone. For some, the damage is already done when they can’t afford to pay for groceries at the checkout. It’s clear and straightforward: if they truly wanted to provide a genuine free trial, they could do so without these financial traps. They could charge everyone fairly, regardless of their ability to pay upfront. My advice? Exercise caution and think twice before getting involved with this app.
author: BOK Karl

title: £199 for an App!
body: Spent 10 minutes answering questions before you get to the part where they want to rob you
author: ADHDDAN

title: Ridiculously expensive
body: £33 a month is just too much
author: XXChris

title: An hour in and I’m ready to cry
body:
There are many issues with this app right from the start. They create roadblock after roadblock that any neurotypical would be able to navigate with ease but for us neurospicy individuals it’s like walking over hot coals, while trying to carry a car, In a crowded room with everyone talking. LOUD. 

Once you have downloaded the app you have to go through the signup process and there we reach the first roadblock. I have to pick a username, out of thin air, with no context of how it will be used. 

The app won’t let you continue without picking one, they won’t assign a random one for you, you have to create one. Without any limits or rules displayed. 

If you make it past this point (which took me nearly 15 minutes) you then have to agree to either a yearly billing or monthly billing. And yes I know they say there is a 7 day free trial and also if you forget to cancel they will refund you but do they not release we have RSD. 

Just the idea in our own heads that we may be rejected for a refund will make us not ask for it. Yes I know they guarantee it no questions asked but we still think it’ll get rejected (that’s why it’s a dysphoria). Another thing you think they would understand since the creators claim to have ADHD themselves. 

Moving in from that and this was the last straw for me. To be able to do anything in the app you HAVE to watch a video of a guy talking to you.  NO NO NO NO NO. I immediately shut the app down and uninstalled it. 

To say this app is supposed to have been created by neurodivergent developers it’s my absolute nightmare and looking at other reviews I’m not the only one.
author: Yorkshire Hot Tub Services

title: This app changed my life. Seriously.
body: After i got ADHD diagnosis it felt great to have an explanation for why things in my life are the way they are but then i had to take action. This was paralysing. I watched YouTube videos and spoke to people on Reddit but only made small amounts of progress. This app is a gem, it has loads of educational content and an ADHD coach who is amazing. She doesn’t answer back immediately but it’s fast enough to not be an issue. I will be a lifelong user!
author: plandrover1

title: Ok. Expensive & Coaching is not good for the price.
body:
I like to community aspect of this app. I like the courses that you can do and the zoom ‘drop-ins’. However the big USP of this app is the personal coaching. 

This is why they charge £170 per year. However the coach I had would send scripted sentences about setting goals about 2 days after I sent them a message. 

I was struggling at one point and didn’t respond to a few messages and haven’t heard from them since (about 4 months ago), no check-ins, or queries about how things were going. Nada. 

I like the idea behind this app. However I do feel like I’ve paid hugely over the odds for what is essentially a few very brief 5 min Education courses.
author: DocTrimKyte

title: Great app
body: App is great and I loved my free trial.. sadly out of my price range to pay for a annual or monthly fee at this level.
author: skabo1982

title: No free version
body: In order to open this app you have to commit to a paid expensive contract. There is no access to this app without first agreeing to subscribe. It would be better to provide limited access for free and allow people to opt in to the paid service rather than forcing a subscription that has to be cancelled on people who are trying to get help with organisation. Seems like an unfair and very expensive trap to me. I deleted it immediately as I know I’ll forget to cancel. Plus it’s not worth it if you only get 1 week free.
author: Metsuzy

title: Rip off
body: Won’t even let you start without a 7 day trial and then charges £50 a month!!! Absolute rip off.
author: velleity18

title: Deleted the App!
body:
Downloaded this app before founding out it costs £180 per year to use. 

As there is only a 7 day free trial to see if this expensive App is worth all the money (not long enough) and knowing I will most likely forget to cancel if I don’t find it usefull - I have decided to delete it before even getting started. 

I have no problem paying money for something that’s good but how do we know unless we’ve tried it out.

If you are truly confident in your App - make the free trial longer - 30 days - and this is the most important thing you need to do - DON’T TAKE ANY PAYMENT DETAILS UNTIL THE END OF THE TRIAL. You will then gain trust from the beginning and more people will try it out. 

If it’s good we will pay. If not we won’t. What you are doing is unscrupulous for people with ADHD - you are taking advantage of the people you are supposedly helping. Shame on you.
author: MonkeyPuzzler

title: Way to expensive

Very expensive, overwhelming start and with Adhd good chance of forgetting to cancel the free trial and rolling over. Was put off sorry! Would be happy to pay a monthly fee but at this price to big of commitment.
author: Em-Gracie

title: Not helpful at all
body: Going in, I expected this app to try and support my short attention span, improve my focus and generally help with my symptoms of adhd. The layout of the login process was not clear at all, complicated, hard to navigate and time consuming. The app does not let you in unless you commit to a 7 days free trial, at the end which the app will automatically start charging you if you forget to cancel. They do say that they’ll refund you if you forget to cancel, but as with a lot of other apps, verifying such things can be incredibly time consuming and complicated, not something that people with adhd need to deal with. Please devs, if you actually want to help people like myself at all, change the login process! I deleted this app pretty soon after getting it and will not be redownloading.
author: LangleyHQ

title: Terribly expensive
body: Super slow and downloading it was a pain for the constant updates
author: garavatito

title: Do you even know how adhd people suffer? Doesn’t appear so.
body:
I have 2 major issues from the get go with this app. First, it’s too expensive, the majority of people with adhd struggle with our finances as a result of impulsive or inattentive behaviour, when I looked at reviews they were saying £20 a month £90 a year, and I thought that was ok, only to go through sign up and find it’s double that, £43 a month or £180 a year. £43 is what I spend on my whole food shop for a week for my household of 2! No app, which has major limitations and cannot replace actual coaching, especially for a condition where accountability is a major driving issue, is worth that much money. They say it’s to replace in person coaching but frankly, you can not to open an app, you can ignore reminders, and more often than not they become wallpaper as they mix with all the other notifications on your phone. You can’t ignore a person who is actually stood there asking how something went. Plus when looking at reviews the things that might make it worth the exorbitant cost are not in my time zone.

Second, Promising to refund people who forget to cancel isn’t good enough, you should have a free trial that is actually free, no payment details taken until the trial is over. It’s shocking that as you claim to have adhd yourselves you don’t do a trial where no details are taken, and knowing that the majority of adhd people will 1. Forget to ask for a refund, and 2. Procrastinate on it when they do remember because it’s so much painful admin is predatory and frankly disgusting. Of all people you should know how hard it is to remember to cancel at a time that you can actually cancel, and not remember while you’re washing up or driving the car, and you should know that as time goes on people are going to build a wall of awful around cancelling. 
If you actually believed your app was as good as you claim and wanted to be inclusive you would be like sunsama, have a 14 day free trial where people can try it without having to give you payment details or set up a payment, then they try the app and love it and find it useful so they then pay. If you’re so sure your app is so great what have you got to lose? Surely everyone who tries it will want to pay for it because it’s so amazing it’s worth spending the same amount I spend on groceries every month?
Alternatively you could set it up so that if the person doesn’t use the app for say 5 days in a row, it automatically cancels and refunds them, why don’t you do that instead of manipulating the very condition you claim to support?
author: GECarr

title: Amazing tool for recently diagnosed adult with ADHD
body: Inflow is so much more than just another ADHD app. Yes, it is expensive, but definitely cheaper than going to an ADHD coach or seeing a therapist even once a month. It’s a personal, real person, qualified coach who you can reach out to about questions or for accountability. It’s a resourceful place with plenty of useful modular courses on subjects such as acceptance, women and girls with ADHD, relationships, procrastination, etc. Everyone of them broken into short texts with audio recordings (by a human) of around 4-6 minutes. You can listen to/read one each day, reflect on it in a little text box after (if you want to) and get some helpful tips that you can save for future reference.    This app also offers live video links that you can join to keep you accountable and on-task when you want to accomplish something (homework, chores, work, etc). There are also live video discussions with psychologists and other specialists that you can join on various subjects. These are so helpful to see that you are not alone! And the community section as well where we can exchange on struggles and successes. Finally, you get several challenge ideas and guidance to learn new tactics, improve some habits or routines, etc. One thing though, I noticed that the “Daily Flow” isn’t there anymore. Please bring it back! It’s one of the best things in Inflow! It is what gets me motivated to open the app and gets me started on the modules. If you won’t put it back on the home page, can we have a way to access the previous ones? I have tried many guided meditation/reflection apps and this is the best for me. Thank you Dr. Sachs and the Inflow team!
author: M-E_D

Yes it’s true that ADHD treatment is much more expensive but you also get much more from that. So I hope that they reconsider the price or offer some kind of discount options.

body: So much to say about this app, but the conclusion is to get it.

title: Forgot to cancel my free trial
body:

author: Shenmee

title: Love it - great app just what I’ve been looking for to help with ADHD
body:
This app is really useful and informative as   not only does it teach you ways to manage your ADHD  using prompts and daily journal planning and challenges to help motivate you to progress  it has videos of events  with discussion issues such as anger  management and  getting things done ..with invaluable advice  from people who care.  I am   currently trialling   it got a bit longer and not sure what I would do without it  ..the annual subscription is a little high  until you think about and realise what is being offered. So I think I will just have to buy less stuff! It might help if there was a quarterly or half yearly option though?  If you have ADHD there  is no harm in trying the app for  free week  to see what I mean (although  there is more content-than you    can do in  just one week ) You    can also always cancel the subscription before the renewal date without any issues.   
Thanks   inflow for  this unique app  Love it

author: Christiesixfivesix

title: Tone is not quite right.
body:
Now that the technical issues have been fixed, I’ve had the chance to give this a go. The structure of the app and chunking of the information is great. I love that there are both video and text options. The information itself is brilliant… and there are definitely techniques that I could learn and use to help manage my time and support my organisation. 

However, the language used is disappointing, and the tone is not quite right for me. In one section alone there is reference to “messing up”, “screw ups” and “weakness”. Not everyone’s experience with ADHD has been negative, and I’m not sure how helpful this narrative is.
author: Icclemoose

title: Also disappointed
body:
Highly infuriating that I wasted time signing up and answering questions to them be met with a monthly subscription fee sign up after 7 days!
Sick and tired of subscription services on apps now and if I’d of known this from the start I wouldn’t of even downloaded this app!
author: LilRockit

title: Disappointed
body:
I really hate when you download an app that does not state that if you want to use it at all, you have to enter into a yearly subscription (nearly £90). Yes you get a 7 day free trial but as someone with ADHD, I often forget to cancel these and then end up paying for something I might use. Also, I had to go through the whole verification/account set-up process with emails and confirmation codes and emails that take too long too arrive so that was super frustrating and made me wonder if the developers actually know anyone with ADHD or realise how frustrating these kind of multi-step processes are for someone with ADHD. 

So I never got to use the app, but if these basics aren’t right for someone with ADHD then how good can the actually app even be!
author: MummyMelsa

title: Useful practical help
body: I’ve only used this app for the free trial so far but I’ve really enjoyed it. The daily coaching is full of useful tips and these are presented as challenges to motivate you to complete it. The app is really accessible - at first I was dismayed that the coaching session were audio but there’s options to alter voice speed and there’s a text instead option, and all the sessions are short and concise and summarised at the end.
author: Ixuxia

title: Good if you aren’t in therapy/don’t have other resources
body: I was hoping that this app would offer helpful routine/time management things, like letting you plan a routine, timers/reminders, offering resources on how to develop and stick to routines, etc. That’s not really what it’s for – it’s basically a therapy programme which has a journal & a space for you to write what you want to focus on every day. The therapeutic resources are OK – I imagine there are probably a few things in there that I didn’t already know, but I’ve covered a lot of it in CBT, DBT and other therapies I’ve done or read about independently. So if you’re a beginner to emotional regulation, time management, etc. and/or just want to put some work in across the board, it’s probably good for that, but it’s quite beginner-level so I won’t be paying for the full version after the trial. A lot of potential and I’ll be keeping an eye out for updates, but this version didn’t offer me anything new.
author: nickyjwatkinson

title: Life changing
body: This is a great app and programme, and unique as far as I can tell. It is helping me get to grips with some of the most frustrating and paralysing aspects of ADHD in a way that I have not been able to do with other resources. It’s divided into small sections which I find perfect for my attention span - on most days I simply can’t take in more, and I find I can apply the tips and suggestions given quite easily and effectively. Sometimes I forget all about the app but then after a few days I return and pick up where I left off - there’s no pressure. Finally the app is also special because it is interactive, not just a bit of inanimate  software. The developers are clearly engaged and present, including through live Q&As with the experts. Many thanks to the creators of this app.
author: Rakooo9771xx

title: Amazing
body:
I joined inflow in a time where I was at my lowest and had no idea what to do with myself or how to act especially since my adhd has just been getting out of hand and too overwhelming. Inflow is truly amazing and honestly makes me feel so much more confident with my adhd and mostly, makes me know that I am not alone and heard. I actually really love the Q&A as it makes it more personal and allows me to get an answer from a professional and not just google, as well as hear other people’s questions which may be useful for me too. 

The modules are really helpful especially with the challenges they provide, it actually makes me have to do the thing rather than just listen to something and never try it. It also helps keep things exciting for the adhd brain because completing a challenge or a module is just exciting and makes you feel like you did something that day.

However, one thing I would say is that is that I wish others could access this app without having to pay. I fully understand that the creators worked really hard for this and dedicated so much time, effort and money to make this and they also have bills to pay however some people may really need help just like I did when everything just got too overwhelming for me. I was able to get some help from this app but others may not be able to depending on their situation which really saddens me. However I wish that in the future this app could become free or even allow some people (depending on their situation and financial state) to access this app for free. I truly think that anyone should be able to get the help they need when they need it which is why I hope something could be done in the future.

Overall amazing as an app and I fully support it and would definitely recommend!

title: Misleading.
body:
At first glance this app looks great. A free app with great reviews, for people with ADHD that are trying to get their lives in order.

During onboarding I get to tell you about myself and choose how I’d like to be supported. After setting up an account I’m presented with a screen telling me that nothing is free. Nothing can be tried and no help is available –unless I agree to spend as much as £25. Every month!

It can’t be dismissed and I have no way of removing my account. This is the most misleading and underhand of approaches. After such high hopes it seems only those that have plenty of disposable income get help.

Find out how much people can really afford to pay. A private diagnosis and titration (given overstretched and under commissioned NHS services) costs around £1000. An extra £300/year for this app (on top of prescription costs) is exclusive, discriminatory and desperately unfortunate.

I’d like to remove my account, and all the answers I provided, from your systems.

title: Request for Refund Due to Unintentional Subscription
body:
Dear [App Support Team],

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to bring to your attention an unfortunate incident regarding my recent subscription to your ADHD management app. Due to my condition and the challenges associated with it, I inadvertently failed to cancel the subscription, resulting in an unexpected charge.

As someone who struggles with attention and executive functioning difficulties, managing my expenses and subscriptions can be quite challenging at times. I understand that it was my responsibility to cancel the subscription before the renewal date, but I genuinely made an oversight in this matter.

Upon realizing the charge, I immediately requested a refund through the appropriate channels. I would like to kindly request your understanding and assistance in processing the refund as soon as possible. The charged amount poses a significant financial burden for me, as I am unable to afford an unplanned expense of this magnitude.

I must emphasize that charging customers without prior notice, especially considering the nature of your app, which serves individuals who face challenges with attention and executive functions, feels somewhat unfair and even abusive. I sincerely hope that you can empathize with my situation and take it into consideration while reviewing my refund request.

I assure you that I did not make use of the app during the period for which I was charged. It was an unfortunate oversight on my part, and I apologize for any inconvenience caused by this matter. I am hopeful that you will understand the circumstances surrounding my situation and grant my request for a refund.

Thank you for your attention and understanding. I look forward to a prompt resolution to this issue.

Yours sincerely,
Mary

CBT as a treatment has been questioned, with declining efficacy rates and quite nasty potential side effects. 
ADD is no longer a clinical term, and I’m pretty sure it’s been out of professional circulation since like 2014 or something.

title: Scam
body:
I think this app could’ve been useful long-term. I decided to try to use it for the free trial period to see if the subscription was worth it. I enjoyed the app, and as an ADHD-er does, I committed to it for a day and forgot it was there. Great tool with great resources.

Here’s where the scam part comes in. Since I forgot the app was there, I decided to cancel my free trial. I appreciated the reminder email. However, it took me THIRTY MINUTES to figure out how to cancel. I would describe myself as a tech-savvy individual, so that is quite ridiculous. Can’t cancel on the app. I like to believe the best in people, but I perceived this as deceptive, particularly for someone with ADHD. I followed the link to cancel the subscription provided in the email. Leads me to sign up for and download another (unrelated) app called Notion, which is not only so confusing but incredibly sketchy. I tried the link 3 times, even on a different device to see if it was some error. Nope. So I went along with it, created an account and downloaded the app and whatever. I searched and searched the app for ways to cancel my Inflow subscription  - had NOTHING to do with it. Finally, I had to rely on Google. I finally found an online link to cancel my subscription. 

This shouldn’t be this hard. I found this deception to be quite disgusting and degrading. Be better, please.

title: I deleted this app within hours of starting the free trial.
body:
I use unique email addresses and phone numbers for every service I sign up for so I can identify when my information is shared or misused. Less than four hours after creating my Inflow account, I received a text message on the phone number that I had only ever used for Papa John’s. While I can’t say with certainty how it happened, the timing was concerning enough that I no longer trusted the service with my data.

What made things worse was trying to delete my account. Instead of providing a straightforward in-app process, I was directed to a Notion page to request deletion of my data. It felt unprofessional, was unnecessarily difficult to navigate, and didn’t inspire confidence that a company handling sensitive personal information takes privacy seriously.

Based on my experience, I won’t be using this app again.

title: “Free trial” scam
body: I have no idea how I signed up for a three month free trial. I didn’t have any sign up emails or even a log in/password but just randomly got charged $200. author: hrstrt

title: Predatory Scam
body: Avoid this app at all costs.  They have double charged me and many other users.  They do not answer any queries through their email. Despite multiple attempts to contact them at the only available email address on their site, they have not replied after two months.  There are better options available that do not prey on users. title: Second Best Time is Now
