My favorite part is the measuring progress over time in areas that I struggle with. I wish I had found this app sooner, but second best time is now!
author: 👽E.T.⚡️

title: So so
body: It’s not bad. I have learned a few things along the journey so far and I think knowledge is half of the battle. Especially if you just found out you have ADHD. Some of the tools are not as useful. I paid for the Quinn AI and I think it is probably helpful if you use it to work through things. I have found that I don’t use it very often. I paid for the archetype test and while it is spot on in some areas there are others that are completely inaccurate. There is no way to take the test again which kind of sucks. The other community based tools are interesting but it doesn’t have an open section where you could throw out something you’re struggling with and have the community respond. Overall, I like it but I don’t know that I’ll renew once the subscription comes back around.

author: Luvthisong751245

title: Predatory billing and exploits ADHD symptoms
body:
I signed up for a free 7 day trial in May 2024. The app will redirect you to enter payment information on their website so the billing date will not show under your app store subscriptions. If you cancel before the end of the trial period you immediately lose access to the app. Inflow also does not send an email when they bill you. I have paid $600 for an app that I used for less than a week over 2 years ago. Inflow takes advantage of people diagnosed with ADHD because we are more likely to struggle with forgetfulness and staying organized. 

Even if you do remember to use the app, it contains tips that you will see on any other ADHD app or blog and the layout of the app is not engaging. 

Living with ADHD has made me feel like I am inferior to my peers many times in my life and getting duped by this app certainly did not help.

title: all talk and no walk
body: this is an app that masquerades as an ADHD help app. you are given a one week free trial, which for me, someone with real ADHD, is just about enough time to sign up for the trial and forget that you ever had the app in the first place. By the time my trial ended, I have been given no reminders or notifications about anything relating to the app. Seems like that would be pretty standard for an ADHD help app. Even worse is that once the trial ends, you are totally SOL. It’s pay up, or get lost. They have some funnel where you can apply for a student scholarship or a free donation subscription. I’m a student and I applied for both. I never heard back from either. This app is the epitome of talking the talk and never getting off the couch to walk the walk. if they actually wanted to help people with ADHD it wouldn’t be so money focused.

author: SerenaJE

title: ADHD is ME? I didn’t want to believe it.
body: All I have to say about this App is “wow! I have been a very high functioning woman my entire adult life and very successful in school before that. I had no idea I was so high functioning that I was masking my ADHD tendencies. Now in retirement, I can see it clearly that I need structure, a lot of self-care and self forgiveness, and finding new ways to function in my world. ADHD looks different in women. I didn’t want to believe I could have this label, but now that I see clearly how I have the tendencies, I have become much more forgiving towards myself. That self understanding and self-care energizes me as I adapt  to retirement —using the learnings of this app. I will continue to go back over the lessons here because they are so important to my well-being.

author: gunnierto

title: It works!  I’M LIVING PROOF!
body: This app WILL help us build new routines and rhythms!  We can do it, one step at a time… commit to using this app and building a new rhythm of life and you’ll start to see changes.  I am proof of that.  This app is a teaching tool, it’s not exhaustive but it’s the most practical I’ve come across, and I’ve looked through everything available.  Inflow App is realistically structured.  Lasting and REAL growth with any program is slow progress.  Try to ignore the impulsive reviews, those folks weren’t desperate enough or ready to partner in the ownership-engagement-process - most negative reviews seem “victimy”.  We must do more than merely click through the lessons and think change will unfold, we actually have to figure out how to implement the suggestions in a way that words for us individually.  Create a system, I’m using MS OneNote on my iOS device to create checklists (AM Routine, Daily Routine, PM Routine, etc.).  Use a whiteboard, sticky notes, a written or digital checklist, etc. George and the Inflow team is giving us the tools and it’s on us to use them - like anything else in life.  Don’t over-complicate it but gather the tools, take in the good, the useful for you, set aside the rest and get to action!  One step at a time!

title: Fabulous help & fun!
body: The zoom sessions are the best! This is where myself and others with ADHD (ADHDers) rock our projects, work , etc. out.  There are 25 minutes where we focus and then a 5 or more minutes break for encouragement and sharing (no pressure to share). The moderator I am with the most is Callie, who is also an ADHDer. She has tons of experience and is extremely down to earth, motivating and helpful. She has us pace ourselves and listen to what is needed - a meal, a rest, a way to understand what is going on and helps us, etc. This is something needed b/c the executive functioning of our brains is not the same as others. There is no pressure on zoom, but there loads of great ideas. There is an electric air at times as we champion each other and when there are days when I or others of us is struggling or down, we offer each other encouragement. I have seen that this really boosts the results - it amazes me how much we all get done. The more I attend, the more I get done and live a more balanced life - it is accumulative, even though there are some up and downs. The zoom sessions are so satisfying and we also have a lot of laughs. Besides the zoom sessions, there are around 45 or so topics in mini lessons, available as well. Having an understanding of many aspects of having ADHD and ways to succeed, our strong and weak points has allowed me to move forward in my life. I was diagnosed many years ago but didn’t have the tools and knowledge. In addition to the zoom sessions and mini classes, there are questions posted to the community and it is gratifying to understand our common challenges, concerns, and wins. There are people of a wide variety of ages (many youth, I think and others, as well). I believe that if you are a student, you can get a discount. Definitely worth the try!  I have been doing this since a year ago, last July. PS I was first skeptical that the 25 minute focused sessions with 5 minutes off would work for me and felt I sure I would not like it.  I gave it a try, early on, however, and am amazed and so thankful.

title: Therapist Approved!
body:
I work as therapist and lot of my clients have been presenting with ADHD, and I’ve recently discovered I have it too. This app has been so great for lots of reasons. 

1. It’s a great way to start the morning on the right intention (bite sized learning and reminder of what works for us and what doesn’t. Rather than getting stuck in doomscroll early in morning and derailing the day). 

2. The app tailors your adhd learning to your specific areas of struggle via quizzes. 

3. The information your learn is very adhd brain friendly and bite sized chunks so as not to be boring or overwhelming. 

4. Great community aspect - daily reflection questions that people can answer and respond to one another on. And body doubling co-working session opportunities. 

5. More modules to explore if you want to go at a faster pace and learn more on various topics - Relationships, productivity, time management. Etc 

I use it and love it. Several of my clients have tried it and love using it as well to manage the adhd and learn about it in between sessions.

title: Maybe useful if you were just diagnosed/have never been to therapy? Regardless, not worth the $
body:
I am trying to be charitable here! I have ADHD, it was diagnosed 5 years ago, every now and then I download a productivity or ADHD help app or whatever because… I have ADHD, so it’s hard not to lol. And inflow is different from most stuff like that! 
In that it! Kind of isn’t anything! The features are incredibly limited, the ‘modules’ are interesting as a concept but are just someone reading facts to you (or you can read them yourself) that are so basic they’re not even ADHD 101, they’re more like. Pre-calc? Anyway it won’t be anything you haven’t heard before if you’ve ever had a therapist for longer than a few weeks. There’s no way to take notes and no like, guided anything (the coworking thing is cool though). I appreciate the concept of having CBT resources all in one place if you’re super new to the scene, and the list of ‘brain hacks’ (that language should be a tell that this isn’t really gonna be useful but oh well, one always hopes) is fine as a resource I guess, and if I stretch credulity a little I can imagine that the creators maybe don’t want you to be on your phone much? Which, ok? But for the price tag!!!! It’s kind of shameless!! I know Google is broken right now, but seriously there are equally comprehensive programs you could find for free with very minimal digging, and at the end of the day this is essentially paying like $40 a month for the therapeutic equivalent of a stack of picture books and a single sticky note. Just watch a YouTube essay and get headspace or something, at least that will hold your attention for awhile haha. Their refund policy is good though, at least.

title: Literal Life Saver
body:
This app has quite literally changed my life. I was feeling so hopeless after having exhausted several therapy modalities to try to manage my mixed presentation ADHD (along with other diagnoses) but none of these previous modalities ever ended up being sustainable long term or had major gaps in their efficacy due to me being neurodivergent. Many of these other therapeutic modalities don’t take neurodivergence into account when drafting up their content either. Especially when it comes to how we learn and perceive information. 
But now that I’ve found Inflow I’m so incredibly thankful for this app and how powerful it is! This app has clearly been crafted by experts in ADHD neurodivergence. I’ve only been using Inflow for a few days and I’m already majorly blown away at how effective it has been in helping me both gain a deeper understanding of how to manage my ADHD symptoms while also validating my experiences as a person born with neurodivergence. We’re wired differently and that means that it takes a different and specialized approach to assist us in being able to successfully move through a society built for neurotypicals. 

Inflow is 110% worth ANY amount of money needed to keep this therapy relevant and accessible to all. I wish that everyone could hear about this app and how simple and easy it is to approach. The first step toward treatment is often the hardest and now that I’ve started with Inflow I never want to stop working with it. Cheers Inflow team you deserve it!

title: Boring
body: I saw an ad compare it to  Duolingo. It is nowhere near as interesting or engaging
author: Smurfbaws

title: So eye opening.
body: I was recently diagnosed with ADHD. This app has been so eye opening. I had no idea how much of my life this was affecting. Now that I have the awareness it’s so much easier to manage. I’m so thankful I found this app.
author: Wmmuga

title: Read the fine print
body: Predatory ADHD app. I unsubscribed from this app via app store and it did not cancel my subscription EVEN THOUGH THE APP SAID IT WAS CANCELLED.  After $150 of charges I opened the app, confirmed that the app said my trail was expired, checked my account and saw the message that cancellations have to occur on their website.  There should not even be an unsub option on the app store.  If you have ADHD stay away, it wasn’t beneficial, is way too expensive, and is predatory towards a group of people who notoriously have issues managing subscriptions.
author: pygmykat

title: Especially the live events
body:
Inflow has been, and continues to be very helpful for me.  I’ve learned a lot through the modules.  

Having said that, the live/co-working events and the community forum are my favorite parts of Inflow.  The Sunday Setup is my most favorite, and integral to getting my week started off on the right foot.
author: LateBloomer592

title: ADHD Prowlers! Good luck canceling!
body: Downloading this app is the worst decision if you think you might want to cancel in the future. I did the free trial and decided to try it out for a year, which was $200. After I was charged I realized I wasn’t using the app and it wasn’t worth the money for me. So I decided to cancel future subscriptions. However, when I went to my iPhone subscriptions under settings, the Inflow app wasn’t listed. I figured it wasn’t renewing and I wasn’t going to be charged again. Boy was I wrong!!!! I have been charged 2 years in a row after my initial purchase and cannot figure out how to cancel. This app is created for people with ADHD, so these experts should know that canceling subscriptions needs to be easy for its users because having to go through multiple steps to figure out how to cancel isn’t always possible. It’s my belief the app creator makes canceling this subscription difficult to impossible knowing very well that its users aren’t always capable of canceling, therefore they are able to bank on the very people they intend to help. I want my $400 back for the 2 years I was charged and I do not want to be charged for this next subscription coming up in the next couple weeks.
author: ReadJennifersReviews

title: Decent but Expensive
body: Had to cancel because of a layoff. It’s mostly articles.
author: Claire3M

title: Scam!!!!!! Got charged 199.99
body:
I got charged 199.99 for a year long subscription. There is no way to cancel the free trial. I never even set up an account. I don’t understand how this is legal. They do not respond to emails requesting a refund.

This is very unfortunate because it seems like this app is intentionally trying to take advantage of people with ADHD. 

I would give this app negative stars!!!!!!
author: Unbiased-reviews

title: So far ehhh
body: I’m hoping there will be more activities and ways to engage myself and my behaviors in the way that I can in my workbooks
author: Dave Meekins

title: Free Trial Cancellation
body: There is no way to cancel their free trial. I’ve been trying to do so for days!!! The instructions on the app and online keep going in circles… feels intentionally confusing in order to not allow you to cancel! I’d give this 0 stars if I could!!
author: Reviewing Nick

title: Not novel and charges after cancelation
body:
The app is basically the same as other ADHD apps, none of which have been particularly helpful to me.

However, a differentiator is that inflow's cancelation process does not consistently work - so you maybe have the pleasure of being charged even after you cancel a free trial or subscription. For example, I canceled but have been charged $199 at least 2 years in a row. I set reminders to cancel subscriptions like this when I'm trying out an app so there's something fishy with inflow's tech.

If you want to pay money indefinitely for an app you unsubscribed to then I do highly recommend this one :)
author: s..j..m

title: Nope
body: Can’t even try out the app without agreeing to a trial, which leads me to believe that there’s no free version. Not worth the ridiculous price
author: esther.hecks

title: Probably saved my credit!!
body: I struggle keeping up with emails.  Joined Jennica’s coworking session solely to go through emails one morning.  I found a fraudulent use of my name on an account and also a data breach alert MONTHS ago and considered junk.  During the session I contacted the vendor and froze my credit accounts!  Forever grateful for the coworking and Callie’s focus room space!
author: Tene12!

title: Overpriced garbage
body: Read a book instead. This app has nothing to justify the price at all.
author: Leoinorbit

title: Not for severe adhd
body: I’m finding this frustrating and useless. Literally within 2 minutes of opening the app it proved to me that it isn’t designed for people with real, severe problems. I was hoping to use this in conjunction with therapy and other things I’m already doing in attempt to help myself but it’s not starting from the ground up, it’s starting from the 10th floor and I’m in the sub-basement. There are major, glaring issues but to give you some of the smaller infuriating “cute” issues: it asked me which signs of burnout I’d ignored in myself and kept going but it didn’t first say what those signs are. If I ignored them it’s pretty likely I didn’t know they were signs. It also said “put that down in your planner” or some such. Dudes: there’s a running joke with adhd people that we hate planners cuz they don’t work and we’re sick of people suggesting we use one as if we haven’t tried it. The moment it said planner I wanted to rage quit. Planners are super triggering to many ADHDers, silly as that seems. It also told me to check in with my friend group. HEY THANKS FOR HIGHLIGHTING THE FACT THAT I DON’T HAVE ONE.  Haha. But seriously … ouch. Could we make it less depressing? No? I hate this.
author: HorribleSpider

title: Expensive
body: This cost twice as much as Hulu and they make you go through a whole sign in process BEFORE telling you the cost. Also the monthly cost is crazy, $47.99 a month for an app. I would say that app is horrible since I didn’t try it out, just be upfront with cost. It’s so annoying with so many apps they make you go through a survey and sign up process and then it’s like $200 a year. I feel it would be cool to have a discount for students (like what Hulu does) since I feel this would help them the most and they also would be the ones who can’t afford it the most.
author: Just Give Me Any Name IDC

title: Not helpful
body:
Watch out! It’s  easy to get tricked into purchasing a year subscription. 
They don’t give you access to the full library you paid for. Instead, they decide which modules you need and only allow you access to them one at a time. I ended up using it for four days as the modules I had access to were not helpful. but was unable to view other modules.
I feel like I wasted more than just the subscription fee and time as I am more skeptical of programs and less likely to try another in the future.
Thanks for nothing Inflow.
author: Bgan99

title: Not an”in-app purchase” app
body: This is actually a 7 day free trial app and then you’re billed $199.99/ year app.  Really should say this up front before making you answer a lot of questions thinking you’re going to get some benefit.
author: KS-Guy

title: Insane pricing. Not any more helpful than any other option available.
body: Predatory pricing. An app for ADHD constantly giving off distracting notifications to address ADHD which is a struggle with distraction and keeping attention. Not ever going to be into the habit of being robbed for an app that’s not much different than others out there. You can use ChatGBT for assistance and education on the matter as well and it won’t hound you or cost an arm and leg. There are lots of viable, good resources out there that don’t require this much money. If one’s service is this helpful, a month for free would really seal the deal and make it clear it’s worth it. Whenever any app costs THIS much monthly (Adobe products, literally multiple powerful apps, cost less and are tools that make its users money), a free month trial would make it clear if its a solid product worth the subscription and not just a notification bomber which, again, isn’t helpful. Apps that I find helpful never need to bother me many times to use them. I turn to them because they notably help me. It’s hard to forget a helpful tool. Books and audiobooks have the same helpful information.
author: SkylerJune

title: Pay us For help
body:
I want you to know, yes you, the one responsible for monetizing; that you should feel disgusted inside about paying to advertise this ad, not putting an *in app payment disclaimer and not mentioning anything about payment until after all personal information and email has been entered. You are part of the problem with this world. Obviously shareholder profits matter more than results or helping people; therefore I will immediately uninstall and tell anyone who mentions adhd help that they should stay clear of greedy platforms like this. I’ve wasted half an hour of my time and knowing some greedy company now has my information is not making me feel much better about my mental health recovery.

—————
 Thank you, you’ve absolutely confirmed my suspicions that the primary value of to the shareholder, not the individual. If you speak the truth and do not wish finances to get in the way of helping people… then you would obviously not be charging financially for it. 

Absolutely no plans to fix the disgusting business practices by putting a simple disclaimer. How about provide the service for free like your app says, instead of hiding the costs in the responses to comments and behind a sign up. It’s really sick to give people false hope of a worry free product and then just say, oh it’s free at first to console them.
author: Robinhoodlum59

title: Be wary of subscription program
body: If you forget to cancel trial, this company will auto-renew your payments by default and will not notify you of monthly charges. It’s an unscrupulous business practice but borders on predatory when serving ADHD clients.
author: Beanwash

title: Right out of the gate
body:
The intake orders the modules so that you need to move through a few modules to get to content that you actually want. The problem is, it starts me off with so many irrelevant modules that it’s hard to wade through. Hey, I’m already a morning person.

There’s a Tim Ferris-iness to the copywriting that’s off-putting for me. Something like headspace that offers many voice performers would be great.
author: pamelalalala_

title: Pricing is different
body: I looked at this app and liked it especially the pricing. I signed up and was only given an option for $199 for the year not the listed price. I co tasted the company and they said they do not have the non coaching. So now you pay the same amount for non coaching that you used to pay for coaching. Then they said I can delete my account and sign up through the app at the Apple Store to get the $99.00 non coaching price. So I did that and it’s still $199.00. I do t understand why they have done this. Very deceiving
author: Reviewer Jerry

title: Paywall
body: The paywall this is behind is unaffordable for huge segments of the population. Assuming that if I don’t have over $200 right now, that $50 a month is doable is downright ridiculous and tells me how out of touch with most of the working public the developers of this app are. Once again, you only get resources if you have the disposable income. The rest of us peasants can suffer.
author: faedira

title: Worth every dime!
body: Before Inflow, I have never paid for an app since the creation of the iPhone because I felt like it was a waste of money. I downloaded the app and got the free trail to see if this app was actually helpful or just another one of those apps marketed to adhd people but is a total waste of time. Oh my goodness!! I was so wrong! This app is literally changing my entire lifestyle and mentality. Usually I never actually commit to anything and actually complete the task because I lose interest very fast and get distracted easily. With this app, I was on it every chance I got to not only learn about my brain, but literally the gives explicit very simple and short lessons with steps and tips to actually change your life. Personally, I made it even simpler by using Ai to create the lifestyle suggestions the app teaches you  to make it even more simplistic for me so I did not have to use any brain power. This app is revolutionary!
author: CrazySassyCool

title: DO NOT DOWNLOAD, SUBSCRIPTION ONLY
body: I spent 10 minutes logging on and setting up just to find out that the ONLY option is a subscription… and it’s RIDICULOUSLY expensive. $200 a year or $50 a month. Don’t waste your time setting it up. The least they could do is beg for your money up front before you go through all the set up. Money hungry developers.

body: The live co-working zoom sessions help so much. The lessons are valuable as well but to have a group coaching session to pomodoro your way through the work day helps so much.

title: Be careful when canceling…
body: I did not find this app useful at all, but what’s worse is I cancelled the app through my subscriptions on my iPhone, before deleting,and was still charged a month later. This was the 1st time this has happened to me. Make sure to cancel your account through the apps but also, through the email they sent you, because if you don’t do both they will still be able to charge you, even though they just tell you to cancel through the Apps, it’s a scam.
author: HollyGolitly13

title: Slimy sales tactics
body: The sales techniques used to sell this app are shameful.  I want it but won’t buy based on principle
author: Anonymous Coward q

title: Predatory, user-hostile app, especially to ADHDers
body:
STAY AWAY 

I don’t usually write reviews. But this app inspired. 

You be assaulted by an endless stream of quizzes, that are very hard to focus through, and added, time consuming pointless graphics splash screens and glossy nothingness. Users are completely captive to this endless process, and it is extremely stressful for my adhd.  I devoted close to an hour trying to get into this app and became so frustrated I submitted a support request and detailed, fair and respectful feedback for them to approve. 

They didn’t reply to my message content, then they charged me $200, one week after downloading for a trial, and trying my best to communicate with the developers about my situation and asking for help. 

Stay away from this app. It was developed by developers, for developers, without an understanding of what adhd users will actually think and feel. This app will profit off us, inappropriately, because adhders are particularly susceptible to bait and switch predatory pricing tactics. We already had an adhd tax, we don’t need Trojan horse solutions making the situation worse. 

STAY AWAY

author: yana3970

body: This app has helped me so much just in the last six days. I wish I could keep using it, but the price makes this app completely inaccessible to me. I imagine others will feel the same. I thought I was seeing things when I saw the price is $48 a month after the 7-day free trial or $199 a year, both of which are completely out of my reach. This is not a budget friendly app, and I am really said to have to cancel my subscription!
author: ActualWoman12345

title: Learning About ADHD and making positive changes…
body: I am learning more about ADHD. Using the tools and techniques from Day 1 have helped me get back some control. I feel that I finally understand what is happening inside my brain.
author: Jeni Rox

title: Coworking with inflow has been totally life changing!
body: I found this from Instagram and joined the inflow free trial out of curiosity with my recent ADHD diagnosis and can’t believe I have this amazing tool. The coworking sessions with Jennica and focus room with Callie have been absolutely life changing for me. As someone who works from home and owns my own business, I didn’t realize how helpful body doubling and having a community of people to track “to-dos” and celebrate “ta-das” with would be for me. I haven’t spent much time exploring the other tools in the app, but I can tell you the live events are worth every penny that I paid. I can’t even find the words to express my gratitude for their kindness and support in my ADHD journey.
author: Megayn

title: ADHD- making my brain work smarter not harder
body: All kinds of tips and tricks and ways to handle everything from lifestyle to work to keeping yourself organized.  It was worth the money.
author: Mad at the wallpapers

title: Life Changing- even for people without ADHD!
body:
I’ve never been formally diagnosed with ADHD, although I suspect I might qualify. However, I think the lessons in this app are helpful for anyone!
In the weeks since I’ve been using this app, I’ve become much more productive and focused as a stay-at-home/ homeschool mom. Our days are better organized and much less stressful! I’m able to effectively set goals and achieve them! 
I’m also learning about Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria (RSD) and how to stop feeling so anxious that other people with judge me. 
This app is definitely life-changing and well worth the subscription! Lessons are short and sweet, but never skimp on quality advice.
If you’re struggling with ADHD or even suspect you might be a *little* ADHD, I highly recommend Inflow!
author: Red ninja girl

title: Why
body: Why do you need my email? Never passed that part. Also trying to choose just 4 things to focus on, then one in the quiz part was not easy. 3 stars for trying.
author: LifeAsDC

title: I’m so shocked by how transformative it’s been
body:
Despite the safeguards they have in place to avoid this very problem, I ended up purchasing a year-long subscription by accident. I’m so happy that I did. I was mostly interested in the ADHD and hormones module but had to complete 4 other modules before I had access to the rest. This kinda made me rush through the beginning because I wanted to see the rest of the library before the end of the trial period (though I had already failed so that ended up not mattering).
The task avoidance module is what really sold me on the app, I learned so many things that I’m actually implementing (E.g., chunking, RAIN). It’s already changing the way I think (aim for 80% completion not 100% perfection). I’m genuinely excited to do my lesson every day. 
I took of a star for two—probably mutually exclusive—reasons: 1. Locking the library during the trial period is a turn off. I get it for people with little understanding of their ADHD, but there are certain things that I already knew this to wish I could’ve skipped. Though I think I picked the first 4. But I also understand why having all the modules available could be overwhelming (I’m experiencing this rn).
2. Even though I just said I didn’t like the prescribed module order, I wish there were like paths we could choose that would have a stack of modules to follow. Choosing what to focus on gets overwhelming.
author: UtopianCitizen

title: Super charge your super powers w/ this app!
body:
I’m a mental health professional who is also diagnosed as AuADHD.  The UI and pedagogy/manner in which material is presented, its interactiveness and how it gives information in bite sized chunks, yet focuses on both layperson/clinical background, in a manner that makes you feel successful at every lesson you master.  I’ve recommended this app to many clients and friends who have needed it.  

Would be helpful to have an iPad app!  It’s much easier on the eyes to read it on iPad than phone.
author: CAdreams

title: Loved it… but no more speakers anymore?
body:
I really loved everything about this app until they stopped doing virtual speaker events (focusing on different topics each time).
Although I was never able to make it to the the live virtual events, I loved that the app would make the video for the speaker available so that I could watch it when I was able, or watch when I felt needed help with specific topics. 

I feel this app has so much potential, but without the virtual speaker recordings, I am not able to justify the price of the app anymore since the speakers were the tool that helped me most.
author: AmyMB12

title: Confusion with canceling
body: Does not work if you cancel this subscription through the App Store like every other app. Absolutely ridiculous process to try to get this refunded when I canceled it on my end.
author: Potatatoskins

title: Audio option
body: The content is great but difficult for anyone with dyslexia with all the reading to be done. An option to hear instead would make it so much better.

body:
I signed up for the app last night and cancelled immediately after taking a look around and realizing it wasn’t what I needed at the moment. I wake up this morning to a $47.99 charge from Inflow for, what, exactly? My not-so-free trial! 

THIS COMPANY IS A PROBABLY A SMALL START UP THATS RESORTED TO THEFT AND FRAUD TO STAY AFLOAT. Shame!
author: teavea013

title: Scam
body:
Whatever the app may provide, it’s not worth it. This company is a scam. Don’t even download the app to check it out—it will cost you $200.

Update: I did receive a full refund within 24 hours of my request. However, it was still very strange/questionable to be charged a full year after trying the free trial and deciding against it. I wasn’t charged a year ago, have received zero communication from the company, and then a sudden charge? Weird. But thanks for the refund.
author: Jbean77

title: no in-app subscription info for this pricey app
body: At $40 a month, inflow should make it more easy to see your subscription information by showing the details in the app. instead they make you leave the app and login elsewhere. This kind of practice to me seems at best lazy and at worst shady. This app is way too expensive to offer anything but the best service.
author: Garreck

body:

They do not apologize or acknowledge fraudulently charging you. 
They also claim to send you reminders about your subscription which is also untrue. 

Scamming company taking advantage of people suffering with ADHD.
author: Nickname34543

title: Can’t believe I spent $199 on an app that I never use
body:
In all fairness they did warn me when my trial would start end. I could totally kick myself for not canceling. I haven’t used it for
More than 5 minutes….why?? Because I have ADHD and can’t focus enough to make it through the exercises!! Unless you are truly dedicated to using it, don’t  spend the money.

I particularly like the live events. The co-working sessions have been incredibly helpful for me. In fact, I wish there were more of them.

title: Begining Inflow Perks
body: I’m happy about the fact that new insights to my ADHD condition are helping me to accept who I am and have hoped to change to more productive behavior as I continue the program.

title: Don’t download this!
body: Bad customer service and they make you jump through hoops to cancel subscription. There are better apps out there and cost a fraction of the price! Really disappointed.

title: App is fine but

author: Gimp-fin

title: Shameful Withdrawal of a $199.00 YEARS’ subscription
body:
I was excited to try - willing to extend my trial by assuming the $50 MONTHLY would be withdrawn after the week-long free trial was up — Nope, when the free trial was up they withdrew the $199.00 from my account… they assumed I would want the “deal” ever so “kindly” — they DID NOT do their due diligence to ensure that I was informed that once the free trial ended I would be charged $200 for the YEARs’ subscription… just one more company ready to charge the card number I gave them in good faith — only to be taken advantage of : (

Upon trying to reach out to get my money back - there’s no phone number - only an info collecting form on their site & an email address — which they want to allow 48 hours to hear back from anyone… then it’s 5-10 business days to get your $$ back (I have yet to see if that occurs). 

 So their product is alright — but I would NOT recommend doing ANY business with company who’s policies are as such.

Can’t even activate account bc no email received with code so can’t even get in to try app AFTER already giving info to charge my card after trial. Can’t even get in to cancel it so have no way to prevent my card from being charged. Anyone who can help me cancel please reach out immediately 
Brittany
author: Bjdoug01

title: Very High Hopes
body: I just started the 7 day trial and I am excited to see how this turns out. So far the app has been both validating and informative. I have struggled severely with my ADHD for the last couple of years. I don’t know if it has anything to do with the fact that I stopped drinking alcohol or that I am just more engaged in the world due to work and responsibilities but either way I feel like this app is just what I’ve been needing. It’s practical, helpful, and very supportive. Thank you Inflow team! Will be posting updates as I continue with my free trial
author: RogueRavenKing

title: SO helpful!!
body: I found inflow after being diagnosed AUDHD as an adult. I immediately dove into the modules, which not only were educational but extremely validating. They gave me language to characteristics about myself and have helped me develop life-changing coping strategies, habits, and supports. The body doubling sessions have been game-changing, and the community is super welcoming & caring. The app is created specifically for people with ADHD, which I love! The interface is clean and undistracting, the modules are brief (yet still full of helpful info), the font & paragraphs are easy to read, etc, etc. I’ve tried several other apps that claimed to be for ADHD, and it was clear they were just a general apps marketing themselves as such. They were awful & not helpful at all! Not the case with inflow! They also go above & beyond to remind you about cancelling your free trial (bc adhd) and offer a financial assistance program. I’m so impressed I haven’t heard of any other apps doing that! I could go on, but this is always way too long 😅 I couldn’t recommend inflow enough!!
author: RMM_Reviews

title: Game changer
body:
This is an amazing app with a lot of great resources in the modules. But the best parts are the live action components. You get a personal adhd coach which is powerful when you need specific help to navigate setbacks. But you also have access to group activities! These might sound weird but are GAMECHANGERS. Think co-working with others who have ADHD and who get it. We keep each other pushing and focused, and reminders to be kind to ourselves when it’s hard or we get stuck. Callie and the team are fabulous at this and truly helped turn the tide on my overwhelm and anxiety. 

I’ve gone from panic attacks daily to using my tools. I’m not such an angry and impulsive mom- though I am a work in progress. And the app has helped me help my kids navigate their neurodivergent brains too. 

Grateful isn’t the word. It’s been life saving. 

I recently was able to pull myself out of a burnout cycle. Before I had no clue what it was. I’m better because of this safe space.  I’ve met so many great people and this community is invaluable. 

Go sign up. Don’t hesitate. It’s worth every penny if you have it, and if you don’t, reach out for financial support bc they have it! 

The test is accurate and it’s used to guide your modules which is amazing, but it’s the people who care and teach you to love yourself again l, and to set realistic markers for success that matter most of all. 

Do it. Get plugged in. You won’t regret it.
author: Mrsbjtee

title: Diagnosed ADHD….. but never knew!!
body:
Well, reading this info is like I have a spy camera in my apartment, my Jeep, the barn where I live and work part time…. And a spy camera that is scanning my brain…..

I had no idea all these things/issues/topics/behaviors were part of the diagnosis!!!!!  Now I am beginning to see where I really stand in relation to ADHD…..

Right in the middle….. drowning in my unorganized, overwhelmed, procrastinating, hyper focused , afraid to start cause I have trouble finishing….. and it won’t be perfect if I do finish self…. I’m a lefty, I teach at a community college, drawing, and lapidary.
I spend probably 1/3 of my income on things for the students, to make things easier and more exciting.  Dang…. You got me pegged!
author: Intarsia21

title: Great app and great facilitators!

The live co-working and focus sessions that go on for several hours throughout the week have been a game changer for me and so many people. Helping me to focus and also not feel alone. Thanks InFlo!

author: Emilytrinity1

title: Game changer for Adult Diagnosis
body:
This app has made such a difference for me. I normally hate subscriptions, but a year of this was less than 2 months of my medication costs. Worth. Every. Penny. To me. 
I wasn’t diagnosed until I was 23, and I don’t think I really believed I had ADHD until a few years ago. I had to get off my medication when I became pregnant at 29. The more I learned about ADHD, the more I realized that I 100% had it. 
This app made me feel so seen and not crazy ! Just understanding how my brain works and coping techniques has greatly helped my mental health. I recommend this app to anyone I meet who got a diagnosis as an adult.
author: Love this-!

title: It’s definitely a good app
body:
The way the app is structured makes it very ADHD user friendly, the information is good and the way it’s presented allows you to move through the program at your own pace. The lessons are informative and most importantly, the people that are behind this app all seem to have ADHD themselves and to me, that’s important. Nothing worse than having someone who doesn’t know what it feels like to have ADHD, tell you what you need to do in order to overcome obstacles associated with ADHD. 

I used to be a member awhile back and they used to have a message coaching feature that doesn’t seem to be there anymore so that is kind of disappointing. They also don’t seem to be doing as many webinars so I hope that picks up again because after you get through all the learning modules there isn’t much left to keep a person subscribing aside from the webinars and coaching. 

I highly recommend signing up for additional inflow 1:1 coaching. They brought the price down quite a bit so it’s a lot more affordable and the personal coaching is so so helpful.
author: SarahWilks7

title: Difficult Trial Cancellation and High Cost: Be Cautious with Inflow App
body:
I recently signed up for a free trial of the Inflow app, which promised a reminder for cancellation. While I hoped for a smooth trial experience, the company’s approach to cancellation left much to be desired. In hindsight, I knew I needed to cancel something, but I didn’t receive a clear reminder from the app. I tried looking for the app to manage my subscription but couldn’t find any active trials, which led me to assume I had deleted the app and wouldn’t be charged. However, I now realize that deleting this app won’t automatically cancel the trial. The 48-hour reminder email was lost in the void during my days off work, and the reminder notification blended in with several other same-day notifications, making it easy to overlook. As a result, I ended up being charged $199.99 for a subscription I won’t use. While the app itself has potential, I prefer other similar apps like Structured and Routinely. I only tried the app twice before losing interest. I’ve reached out to the company for a refund and hope they’ll grant it. If you’re considering trying the Inflow app, make sure to set additional reminders for yourself to avoid a $200 charge if you decide not to keep the subscription. Inflow could certainly improve its process by making trial cancellation more straightforward and user-friendly.

*** I reached out to the company and a prompt, no fuss refund was issued.

author: mrssdr6

title: Inflow app - serious game changer for my ADHD🤓
body:
I’ve been a member for nearly two years and during that time, my life has changed for the better, all because of Inflow! 

- I love the short but resourceful lessons (my favs: money, emotions, time) 
- The live events is a daily thing for me! Body doubling via focus sessions, Sunday reset (4hours) and mid week reset! 
- Live Education sessions: I’ve learned smart strategies for keeping my momentum or serving my dopamine cravings. I learned how to organize for my brain 🧠 and truly embrace my ADHD. 

There are a lot of resources out there for the ADHD community, but this one satisfies all my needs! I even hired a fabulous ADHD coach from Inflow last year for 4 months, she was amazing, a doctor with ADHD. Another option is daily private coaching via the app, also very helpful. 

When I got diagnosed in 2021, I had so many emotions, but was happy to learn I wasn’t unique with my daily challenges. 

Next step, how can I make my life better? In reviewing advice in Facebook groups, YouTube videos, articles and more, Inflow provides it all! 

Each season I choose one place to focus. 

Thank you so much inflow team, please know you are changing lives 😍

Marquesa

title: This app is changing my life
body:
I knew A LOT about my ADHD and wasn’t sure this app would be any help, but I decided to give the free trial a go anyway. Boy, am I glad I did!

This little app has been more effective than therapy.

It has learning components, applicable advice, and it’s perfectly gamified so you actually WANT to check in every day, but you don’t hyperfocus on it. 

It’s the only thing that has gotten me on a morning routine, helped me stop procrastinating, and I’ve even started keeping my spaces clean.

The best part is that I’m breaking the shame cycle I’ve been in where I think I’m not doing enough or living up to my potential. I am kinder, patient, and more loving toward myself because of this app. 

I know it’s a steep price for an app, but it’s worth it.

Thank you, Dr. Sachs, for creating this resource. There’s at least one life out here that you’ve changed.

body:
I really wanted to love this app. I need it. However, as I got into my free trial, I noticed that the things that appealed to me most, like a coach, were left lacking badly. I go through the questions to match me with the right person, etc. There are only 2 coaches. One or the other. So all the hoopla about matching me to someone for me is not real. They don’t even have both sexes available as a coach. It’s one woman or the other woman. I emailed the Dr. Who was emailing me every few minutes about a session asking questions and got no response.  Reached out to customer service and was told “ Unfortunately we do not have a male ADHD coach. If you are interested in coaching, please move forward with the options we have in the onboarding process. Thank you.” 

I responded that I took my trial over Thanksgiving and didn’t get to use it until we got back and wondered if I could get more time? No response. So I’m out. Great idea and concept that doesn’t seem to work or deliver on everything it says. And that’s sad because as I said, I need a program like this.

author: Marissa Nic

title: Awful ADHD helper
body: You know, in today’s ultra-monetized world, it’s hard to find something not tainted by the poison of mobile phone ads and useless currency. But to make me pay for my mental health with an outrageous fee of $17 a month, is pure and utter evil. When the toxicity of capitalized greed was just for mobile games and social media, that was fine. But when it spreads to therapy and mental health helpers, that should raise a few questions. If Wall Street expects me to pay $17 a month for something I have no control over, I won’t. This app says too bad to the people who can’t afford it, but need the help, leaving them rummage around the App Store for the help they need. What fat cat billionaire thinks people will pay $17 a month for help with a mental problem?! This app is  such proof that there is evil in the world, I’m surprised the app developer isn’t Satan himself. This is ridiculous, and I will not stand for it! Don’t get this app.

author: Joseph Kim Hi

title: Best Body Doubling sessions - why cancel them?
body: I finally found an app that works for me.. I tried a ton of things, body doubling discord, Study Together discord, setting up sessions with friends, having body doubling sessions with my ADHD coach. Was about to try Focusmate but there is such friction to setting up a session, and what if you get a weirdo. Then I found Inflow. My productivity doubled because of the body doubling sessions. I discontinued bc of the price, went back to finding and alternative, and then I caved and paid for a year (there’s a way to pay w/o paying for coaching). Aaah, finally my productivity increased again!!! I especially love the Tessa sessions, great for people on the West Coast. The timer is shared, you can be on or off camera. You state your goal and work with a timer for 25 mins on, 5 mins off. Then you update what you’ve done or comment if you catch yourself getting distracted. Others cheer you on and give helpful tips, including the lovely Tessa. There’s a sense of community. They aren’t well-advertised, so maybe not too many people don’t know about them. But people KEEP COMING BACK. There are regulars, and a sense of community. The only problem was that they didn’t have enough sessions and didn’t cover all the days. And then.. I hear that instead of having more zoom sessions, they’re discounting the ones I most love!! Please, Inflow, don’t do this. I guess I’ll have to find another alternative.

author: Concerned 😩

title: Could be really great.
body:
As someone who could potentially really benefit from this kind of app it’s hard to even bring myself to start the free trial when I see it’s $49 a month or $199 a year that breaks down to $16 a month but you have to pay the full year. Here’s the thing, I (and a lot of other adhd’ers )struggle with money and I have bills that need to be paid because I’m trying to fix what I’ve already messed up. As a stay at home mom, I don’t have the luxury to have the kind of money for an app like this that could help. It’s a catch 22,  it turns into this kind of scenario. We’ll help you figure out how to pay your bills and get organized but you have to pay money that you don’t have because you’ve dug yourself into a hole and that’s where you’ll stay because you don’t have money due to the fact that you got yourself into the hole because of your adhd brain! 
I’m trying desperately to get out of this vicious cycle and trying to train myself and help myself because I am the only one who can help me but then find something I think can work  but can’t when everything costs too much money. You want to help people? Make it more accessible for everyone not just people who have the money! It’s sad that not everyone has the same right to be healthy and be able to get help and tools that they could use. I’m not the only person I’ve met that feels like me. I was told about this app originally on Facebook but had 2 friends tell me about it and I was excited. One friend told me she couldn’t use it because of the amount of money per month (she’s also in a similar boat financially) the other has money and always has and she can afford to use it and it’s helped her because she can afford the help.
 Things don’t change in a week. The free trial should be at least a month. Give people some time to actually use the app and lower the price for the monthly fee and yearly fee! Make it accessible for everyone if you really want to help. If not the company is just getting rich of peoples misfortune and  peoples struggles. That’s not right. I’m sorry to not leave a great review but I know I’m not the only person to feel this way. I’m just saying what everyone else is too timid to say. That’s one thing about my adhd is I can voice my feelings. I’ve learned to break through my silence. I hope maybe this will be able to help people like me who are struggling financially but want to help work on themselves to make themselves a better version.

When I saw the add for this app, they had that AHDH friendly text advertised and I couldn’t figure out how to activate that feature. 
We also get personal coaches but mine flat out told me after just two days of using the app that she was going to be out of office for five whole days of my 7 day free trial. title: The “just right” ADHD app
body:
Brand new to adhd treatment at 56 as well as lifetime skeptic of the self-help zeitgeist, I joined inflow on a lark, intentionally flatlining my expectations and expecting to cancel before the end of the free trial.
Inflow proved me wrong on multiple axes and I’m eight weeks past the free trial. If that isn’t teaching an old dog new tricks, maybe I’m not that old.

Inflow provides a number of opt-in support modalities for different learning styles: audio, reading, one on one counseling via chat or phone, a social community, journaling with journaling prompts, group support and group work sessions. Use one or use them all, choose the one that’s right for you or mix and match. 

Well done, Inflow!

author: LizzyBeignet

title: Critical Need for this App! Life changing..Make discount info explicit
body:
I'm taking the time to provide you with feedback related to my experience with inflow. The only complaint I have is my coach was never available during my subscription so I missed out. 

I have suffered with ADHD my entire life but was not diagnosed until my late 20s. The negative self talk is ingrained and the app helped with that pertinent information. 

This app changed my life in a short time. My concern is that the access program and student discount information are not explicitly stated when you sign up. I fear that people who need the service may miss this opportunity. 

Also, financial challenges occur by happenstance especially with ADHDers. I am facing a financial hardship but I at one time had a paid subscription. Making the access program open for people in crisis might help. Maybe with the support of a qualified mental health professional or the like. Maybe a month at a discount or including information under access to help ADHDers learn to manage their finances. You have an amazing opportunity to change lives. 

Have you considered an ambassador program? I say this because I would suggest this app to everyone I know with ADHD. I am faculty at a university, and I believe me and our personalized learning center could promote this service. Nonetheless, I am thankful for the time I was able to participate.

title: The most information I’ve seen.
body: I got the free trial for inflow. I’m originally from a Spanish speaking country, I always had access to tons of physiologists and doctors growing up. However, even though my parents had a hard time with me most times nobody was able to tell them why I had such a hard time with “small” things or habits they tried to teach me. I would forget to do things often that they just couldn’t understand how to the point they thought I was ignoring their requests on purpose. When I finally realized that it was adhd and I talked to a physiologists on my adulthood about my suspicions, they just asked me a few questions and that was it. I was officially diagnosed. However, I never got any tips or tricks on how to manage my struggles with procrastination and just in general. After the free trial I was able to learn so much more about why I can’t get things done. I really wish I could afford the year fee so that I could  learn more.

title: Game Changer
body: The Inflow app is a must have app for the ADHD brain. I’m a huge fan of CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy) and inflow has created a platform to not only teach this specific for ADHD, but has also created a community of people I can relate to who struggle in a similar way that I do, who are learning tools and techniques to deal with the different way our brains are wired. It’s a community where I feel seen and accepted. I have a coach inside the app who checks in with me and helps hold me accountable. There are “co-working” sessions that I can log into and work along with other people who are trying to get work done. The information in the different modules are hugely helpful! I love applying what I learn in the app to my life and seeing how these tools and techniques really can make a difference in the efficiency of my life in general. If you struggle with ADHD, download this app NOW! And I’ll see you inside :):)

The inflow app is a cognitive burden that hurts - not helps - and they won’t return the extraordinary amount of money they charge once you’ve realized this. The coaches aren’t really helpful and the group accountability rooms are limited, East Coast hours - so good luck if you’re anywhere else in the world.  
Furthermore, Apple is a company that doesn’t care about neuro-divergence or that their increasingly glitchy products cause cognitive decline - and they don’t really care about people more than they care about money, so they won’t be refunding your money either once you realize this doesn’t work.

title: Subscription process needs to change.
body: I like your app. I am a mom to several grown children/teens who would greatly benefit from your app. Your process of automatically charging after the 7 day trial needs to change. You sending reminder emails isn’t adequate for your audience. You know and I know the vast majority of people with ADHD have issues with automatic subscriptions. Do the right thing, ask for money to continue after the trial period is over instead of automatically charging it. You guys are obviously talented. How hard is it to pop up a button after the trial is over to say “if you’d like to continue please pay to subscribe”? This would be far more equitable to your target audience. title: Life upgrade
body:
I know many are very well educated on life with ADHD. I like to think I am getting there too 😄. I was diagnosed 2 years ago at age of 37. I’ve been using this app for about 6 months now (on and off, of course 🤪). It is actually very easy to pick back up again wherever you left off, even if it’s been a few days or weeks (or months). 

Anyways, I have found the learning modules really valuable. I think you may too. While not every learning module lesson is directly applicable to me, many of them are. I find nuggets of wisdom that continue to improve my life each time I use it. Sometimes all I get is assurance that it’s ok to be kind and accepting to myself, and I need that too!

The app also has a cool feature where you can time chunk work/breaks with a live group of people. This has been helpful on days when I’m not motivated to do anything at all. You can interact if you want to. Sometimes just having a common goal with people nearby (or virtually in this case) is all I need to stay on task. 

Finally, there’s also some community aspect where you can share your thoughts/struggles/tips for the day and people always respond with thoughtful or encouraging words. I love it!

They charge about $20 a month for access to all this stuff and I think it’s worth every penny. Have I made a good enough case for you to try it (or maybe try it again)?

If I could do a free trial for only the “Understand your ADHD” and “Thrive with new tools and habits” portions without the “Coaching by ADHD Specialists”, I would be in, and probably convert to annual subscription for that. But I cannot see how to do that through the signup process for a free trial even after reading the lengthy Terms. So frustratingly, I am not moving forward. 
I anticipate the app is great but I do not want a coach and have to interact with someone directly.

title: Helpful but overpriced.
body:
There are a lot of great articles and suggestions on self reflection and how to change your thought processes. However, in 3 out if the 7 days fir the trial, I have heard from my “therapist” once. There is a pretty picture but the “therapists” single message was auto bot quality. 

The company claims it’s so expensive because we have access to these therapists. Maybe they are helpful but 7 days is not enough time to find out.

So. I will not be continuing after my free trial because I don’t see enough here to justify the cost. 

My suggestion for the developers is to have the following on top of the current program.

A free version where you can only work on 1 unit in 1 section a day. (There are five different sections with multiple units and I am working on 2 at a time) without access to the therapist.

Two a less expensive version where we have access to everything except the therapists.

This way people can use the program to get help despite their financial situation.

author: Mapawe

title: PREDATORY - read to learn how they use their knowledge of ADHD struggles against you
body:
I don’t say say this lightly but the makers of this app are evil, manipulative scum. Harsh? -  read exactly how they use our disability against us. 

They understand how ADHD people suffer so they use our pain to write the ads and the sign up process.  This get’s you to enter personal info because it make you think if they understand me so well they’ll have the solution i so desperately need and there is a “free” trial. 

To get the “ free” trial you have to sign up for an insanely high priced service at a monthly or yearly rate though.  Which isn’t disclosed till after you’ve come so far and and already started imagining how life would be after this app.  Big sleazy marketing trick. 

You can cancel before they trial ends but they know very well people suffering from ADHD won’t remember too.

They offer two pricing option $50 monthly and $199 yearly. Their marketing targets younger people who don’t have a lot of money so they pick the $50 thinking they’ll cancel if it doesn’t live up to the hype. But remember they already had you paint the mental picture of your life post adhd so the price is nothing in comparison.  If it DID work they would give a much longer no strings attached trial because  no tricks needed if their product really helped people cure their ADHD for $199 a year right!! 

They know very well an ADHD person won’t  remember or get around to canceling or will say next month I’ll start using it.   So they are happy that most will pick $50 and just not get around to canceling. 

Im fascinated by human behavior and do (ethical) marketing as a job.  They are using a very sophisticated but very slimy and despicable process to steal your money.  Don’t fall for it!

author: Dorthyofoz

title: I’d go for it! :)
body:
I’m a licensed mental health therapist that learned plenty practical tips about ADHD here. 

How do you eat an elephant when you have ADHD? Still one bite at a time. This app is a snack, a meal or a buffet you can eat daily in a structured routine or return to when hungry and interested again - highly recommend.

Pragmatic small bites and modules, wonderful (with human interactions from George Sacs who’s terrific ~etc.) live informative events on relevant topics as well as co-working opportunities with a facilitator .  

There’s low key community interaction platform that’s thankfully contained enough to not get lost in like social media and the additional availability of some coaching atvarious price points. There’s no way I give this app less than 5 stars.

I think the change to blue/teal icon is good because pink isn’t for everyone. 

We all have mental health and this app is legit care. No app is a replacement for great personal psychotherapy but that isn’t accessible to many for numerous reasons.

This app offers a powerful adjunct to therapy as well as a stand alone viable too to help support those of us working to manage our own ADHD lives.

How would I improve it? 

I might create an option for accountability groups with a coach instead of individually messaging with a coach. This seems maybe too ambitious to provide sustainable structured coaching for that low of a price annually. (Also, I would not choose asynchronous text for group interactions as that’s hard for many follow.) I’d test zoom like formats with small enough relational weekly groups with break out rooms for two or three people to reflect a specific topic maybe-at a scheduled time with a coach facilitator running it.

Anyhoo- I’ve sent many people to this app who return to me with rave reviews they don’t write here. One, a nurse, spoke of feeling understood and tearing up on break at a hospital on an overwhelming day, relieved to feel so uniquely seen by the apps creators. They were able to find some much new self compassion! Some of the participants in the apps community itself are even remarkably helpful. One recently suggested a (new to me) book that I’ll be introducing to a group I facilitate online! 

As I see it, our future is about fostering community service to one another. This app takes important steps in that direction on a mass scale. It’s helping many. I use it with clients and young therapists I mentor as well.

Additionally, I’ve worked with eating disorders over the years and it’s SO flippin’ hard to recommend anything with nutrition or lifestyle advice on an app EVER- because it’s so common for apps to be a part of diet culture. 

I was so happily surprised to see a friend and colleague, Stephanie Brooks consulted in the lifestyle module. This app development team clearly takes the time and effort to consult with care there-
How RARE and precious!

Okay- time for me to go back to work and I have no disclosures or paid affiliation to say all this stuff. I’m a true fan of this app and all the care that’s gone into it. I’d go for it if your considering an app purchase- worth it!

title: Worth it for a short period
body:
I think this is useful to just explore for a month or so but maybe not an entire year. I did the free trial which helped me explore the app but I don’t think it would be worth it to remain subscribed even with the student discount. I took notes on all the lessons and there was definitely some repetition. For those interested, these are some of my notes: 

1. Get on a routine, waking up earlier, it enhances productivity and energizes you. 
2. Plan your day, break out tasks into chunks to allow yourself time for specific projects
3. Reward yourself for getting stuff done 
4. Make sure your goals are SMART, specific , measurable, actionable, realistic, and timely (set a deadline). 
5. Be compassionate towards yourself and don’t be a perfectionist because otherwise you’re your own worst enemy and you’ll make it harder to be productive. Aim for average, just do a rough draft and iterate and fix it later. Perfectionism or fear of failure leads to an emotional block that can prevent you from getting work done , fear of the outcome or failure and perfectionism leads to overwhelmingly feelings. 
6. Use just one calendar or planner so you don’t lose track of everything you need to do. ( I use reminders for my master list of big tasks and break it down into a daily planner) 
7. Use Pomodoro timers to break work into sessions and create urgency to motivate yourself
8. Working alongside others can help motivate you and force you to focus. 
9. Recognize task avoidance! You might allow your adhd to guide you towards easy, hands on immediate projects instead of focusing on long term ones. Recognizing and naming this behavior helps stop it. 
10. Change locations where you work to introduce variety (this helps with being bored and lacking motivation)  and start projects with what you’re comfortable or good at e.g write out your paper or project as a bulleted outline/list to simply it then fill in the gaps. 

Hope this helps, I like the brain hacks in the app, you can save them and refer back to them.

title: A great idea, but it comes with a hefty price tag
body:
Updated response to the developer: Thanks for your response. I would like to have a little longer to try it. I will reach out for assistance with this. 

Previous review: I gave this application three stars because while I do like the idea behind what it is designed to do, there are some issues that I personally feel should be addressed with the program itself. (Obviously, my opinion may not really matter in this case, but I wanted to offer some helpful feedback that hopefully the developers will consider.) As someone with severe ADHD, I chose to download this from the App Store because I felt that it would be beneficial in helping someone like me to learn to tackle and manage the many issues I’ve struggled with since I was a child. After reading the description, I felt like it would be a good fit for me, and I wanted to try it. After all, even as an adult who struggles with my disability, I still don’t know everything there is to know about my condition and have spent many years trying to understand why I do the things that I do, so obviously, as someone who is seeking more assistance in trying to better myself and my behaviors, this app was quite appealing to me. Not to mention, before you even download it, it presents itself as a truly free app and says nothing about In-App Purchases, which is completely misleading from the start, and I feel that this could come across as a way to get more people to download their app before even reading the full description, but I digress. The description clearly states the cost of the app after the free trial is over. However, while this app appears to have many benefits, and even though I am currently still trying it out, I do not see myself spending the amount of money the developers are asking for, so I have cancelled the Free Trial because the monthly cost is absurd. An application on a mobile phone will never fully take the place of conventional therapy and/or psychiatric services. The reason I say this is because spending almost $50 a month (which equates to almost $600 a year if you choose a monthly subscription) just to get access to a “coach” may be helpful for some, and I’m sure shelling out that much is a no-brainer if someone really wants to throw their money away, but honestly, no app is worth that much no matter what services a company is trying to sell. With that being said, I hope this company really rethinks their pricing scale when they consider how many people could truly benefit from something like this because they stand to lose (and probably have lost out on) plenty of potential customers. The genuine desire to help may be there (and of course, I do get that they may have employees to pay), but asking for so much money from potential customers and requiring a subscription with no free alternative or at least an extended trial so they can truly try everything out before fully committing to it- especially those who are in a vulnerable position in the first place- so that they can get any sort of access to your app is a dishonest practice at best, and while it costs more, I’ll continue to spend my hard-earned money elsewhere on services outside of my phone with real doctors and not on an app that is barely scratching the surface of the services that they provide. So while I do like the app and am in support of the logic behind it, and while I do commend the creators for developing a program to provide their services for free to those who can’t afford them (that is really great and kudos to them!), you are really alienating those of us who might be willing to spend money for the service that you provide at a more reasonable price, and sadly, some people that could truly benefit from what you have to offer will never be able to do that because the price is too darn high.

title: Don't be fooled like I was.
body:
Before downloading to try it out there was a pop up stating that if anything happened and I forgot to cancel before the free trial was over, I would be refunded. It said something like, 'We understand having ADHD would make this really hard to remember, so we will refund you if you forget.' -- something to that effect. That is what pushed me into downloading.

Of course I forgot to cancel the trial and it automatically signed me up for a yearlong subscription ($200). I reached out to support and mentioned the pop-up, casually saying thank you for the refund policy. In response the person told me I need to reach out to Apple first to ask for a refund. I'm currently waiting to hear back from Apple. THEN they will refund you only after you have received a no from Apple first.

But here's the point. The company tries to imply upfront that they have a lenient refund policy BECAUSE they help people with ADHD. Instead, they make you go through the process of asking for a refund from Apple, which for someone with ADHD is another obstacle. What a sham! I went through with it because I was so enraged by the deceit but I know many others won't, and that they make money off this. Shameful.

author: HaraHenry

title: Accessibility still a problem
body:
I really love this app and want to give it 5 stars but the accessibility is a real problem for me. It impacts my consistency of use  because it is so effortful.  Gray and Pink/Blush/dusky rose  fonts are just awful they lack adequate contrast to the white background, thicker font stroke would help. When trying to read I feel like I am constantly straining to see anything. And if you have daylight when trying to use this OY! It washes most of it out 

 Besides the contrast issues I need the option to both increase the font size and view it in landscape orientation as well.  If I could use it on my tablet  and allow it to expand to that size that would be helpful as well! It should be flexible for whatever mobile device you may be using.  

Ideally you would have an option for Dark Mode!! That would be awesome!!! I have dark mode turned on on my iphone but the app does not allow for that user choice. Dark mode can also help with use in bright environments ( e.g., outdoors)

My Favorite features you have: when doing lessons/ programs 
 1. The ability to both listen and read the transcript. 
2. The option to speed up or slow down the audio!  Wonderful accessible options there. 

Please please please. Work on the Accessiblity!!!  I really need to use this app regularly and not be hindered by the fatigue factor!!  You may be surprised how many of us in our 40’s, 50’s, and 60’s may be using this app!! 

Keep up the good work!  I look forward to updating my review to give it more stars.

title: I can’t afford to be a better me
body:
I was diagnosed at a very young age, but my parents hid it from me for 30 years. I often wondered why I have never been able to focus at school or work, often get overwhelmed by chores or tasks other people seem to complete without even thinking about it… I was hoping this app would be a guide to help me improve the areas I struggle with most. I’m sick of always getting passed over for promotions and opportunities because I lack the skills my neuro-typical peers don’t have to pay $200/year to learn. 

 I don’t have the budget flexibility that allows me to justify such a hefty fee every year just to try to level the playing field, but I still decided to give the free trial a go. So far I haven’t seen anything really helpful that made me think this app could be worth such a hefty fee, so I cancelled my subscription ASAP and plan to poke around on it for the remainder of my free trial. Maybe I can find something useful, but so far I’m not seeing anything that would make this app worth so much. 

I have lots of useful apps that help improve my life in different ways. All of which manage to keep their costs well under $75/year. 

Why does an app with such philanthropic claims have such a large price tag? Is this like the Hermès of self-improvement apps or something?

It’s not a hopeless situation that you just have to “try harder” at or continue to push through by yourself over and over again. This is huge thank you so much…

body:

I was formally diagnosed with “sluggish cognitive tempo” for which there isn’t an app (and some cynical people even believe that SCT is a disorder “made up” to sell more psychotropic drugs. Ugh), but the symptoms somewhat overlap with ADHD so the Inflow modules are useful.

Yes, the name “inflow” with the pink colors and the logo that almost looks like a period cup definitely reminds me of menstruation! Strange branding, but maybe there will be a future release that has more attractive graphic design and a stronger logo. Definitely a great resource, so I hope the app continues.

title: Was genuinely excited to see this, however...
body: The cost of this app is absolutely absurd. It's $50/month or $250/year. If you are a newly diagnosed adult with no coping mechanisms, which seems to be the target demographic right now, the chances of you managing your finances well enough to afford this are slim to none. Research has shown, over and over, an increased rate of co-occurrent mental disorders/disabilities, (cyclical) poverty and abuse, incarceration, and stunted academic/educational achievement in the ADHD community. All of these bear direct impact on socioeconomic status. Further, dozens of studies have found correlation between poverty and ADHD. These are the people who can't afford therapy, insurance, and/or medication and who need this kind of help. They don't have $250 laying around or $50 a month to spare. Additionally, if you can afford to offer an annual discount of ~59%, then your monthly charge is not a reflection of your actual operational cost. Again, the ADHDers in need of the help offered by this app are likely going to be in a place where month-to-month is their only option. The lack of any lower pricing options or even a super low-feature free version of the app shows a real lack of knowledge of your target demo, their actual needs, and their likely social location. Now, regarding your link to apply for free access: absurd. First of all, while I applaud your effort, I had to dig through mountains of reviews in order to find out it existed, and I only dug through those mountains of reviews because I wanted to see how many others were as upset by this your pricing structure as I was. Second of all, it is incredibly rare for a developer to offer free access to a very expensive app, and it would never have occurred to me to even see if free access was available. Third of all, I'm successfully medicated and have spent years scouring academic research on ADHD and developing my coping mechanisms. ADHDers not in my situation are unlikely to dig through mountains of reviews. If you genuinely want to help folks that can't afford it, assuming it is in actual application process, make the information readily available and highly visible. Make sure it is included in the articles written about your app. This is just disappointing. /end rant
